b15f6d13a109b466: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi became emotional when he recalled his eight years at the helm of the party, which were marked by hardship and bitter experiences that tested his resilience.
Zahid said Umno had gone through various ups and downs during that period, including wounds that cut deep, but each trial had made the party stronger and more resilient.
"Eight years I have steered the ship of this sacred party. Eight years filled with hardship and tribulations.
"There were ups. There were downs. There were wounds that cut deep into the heart.

"Yet every wound makes us wiser, every trial makes us more mature and every challenge teaches us the meaning of resilience," Zahid said in his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional chairman, said that despite facing various challenges, Umno remained steadfast in its struggle to capture Putrajaya.
He said the struggle was not driven by a hunger for power, spoils or wealth, but by an aspiration embodied in the Blue Malaysia Agenda to ensure the wellbeing of the people and the country.

50dd7f18eaf3256c: KUALA LUMPUR: Singer Aisha Retno has dismissed talk of favouritism surrounding her nomination for Best Pop Song at the 25th Anugerah Industri Muzik (AIM25), following chatter over the song's composer, Ajai, serving as head judge.

The 26-year-old vocal powerhouse, whose full name is Sharifah Aisha Retno Sayed Sipulijam, clarified that all entries undergo a collective evaluation process rather than being decided by a single individual.
"We have many judges, so all nominated songs are chosen through a shared consensus among the panel, not just by the head judge," she said at the recent AIM25 press conference.
For Aisha, having her track Diari Air Mata make the cut is a deeply rewarding milestone, especially given its slow burn compared to her bigger hits.

"I'm very grateful for Diari Air Mata because it's my most underrated song," she shared, highlighting that it is also the sole track in her catalogue she did not write herself, as Ajai crafted it entirely.
Drawing parallels to her earlier single Tak Adil, which also took time to catch on, she remains hopeful that this latest recognition will give the ballad a fresh lease of life.
"I see this AIM25 nomination as an opportunity for more people to get to know the song," she said.
Beyond the trophies, Aisha remains focused on pushing creative boundaries, regardless of how her artistic choices are perceived.
"I know some say my songs are strange, but I only do what I believe suits my style. I do all this for the industry, not just for myself," she added.
Aisha is one of the major contenders with an impressive eight AIM25 nods.

Her nominations span several key categories, including Best Female Vocal Performance, Best Pop Song, Best Electronic/Dance Pop Song, Best Local English Song, Best Album, and Best Traditional Song, alongside self-produced tracks recognised in the Best Festive Song and Traditional categories.
0588528178edc03d: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Former Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa today denied making a U-turn on the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission, saying she had remained committed to the initiative since 2023.

She said a report by a health portal yesterday, which claimed she had reversed her stance, was inaccurate and did not reflect the full context, stressing that efforts on the matter had continued throughout her tenure at the Ministry of Health (MOH).

In a statement, Dr Zaliha said that as early as February 2023, she had publicly stated that the proposal to establish the commission was among the key matters being considered in the final draft of the Health White Paper.

“In fact, in April 2023, the same news portal reported on my meeting with representatives of Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK), where the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission and a Health Reform Commission was discussed within the framework of the White Paper,” she said.

On her parliamentary reply on June 15, 2023, which she said had often been misinterpreted, Dr Zaliha explained that it was a clarification on the scope of authority of a Service Commission under Article 144 of the Federal Constitution.

She said the functions of a Service Commission cover appointments, confirmation of service, promotions, transfers and disciplinary action, but establishing such a commission does not give it the power to create new posts or formulate remuneration systems, including setting more competitive emolument rates.

“I also explained that establishing a new Service Commission would involve a complex process, including the need to amend the Federal Constitution and secure a two-thirds majority in both the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara.

“That explanation was about the structure, jurisdiction and limitations of the model available at the time, and was not an outright rejection of the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission,” she said.

Dr Zaliha cited records after the July 2023 parliamentary session showing that she had publicly confirmed the Government’s intention to establish the commission and was assessing the best model for it.

She said the commitment was followed by the establishment of a Technical Working Group by the MOH in October 2023 to identify the best methods and mechanisms for setting up the Health Service Commission.

Dr Zaliha reiterated that her position on the welfare of healthcare workers had remained unchanged, stressing that any reform of the healthcare service system, including the establishment of the commission, must be implemented urgently and backed by an authority capable of resolving the crises faced by healthcare personnel.

According to media reports yesterday, Dr Zaliha called for the Government to expedite the establishment of the commission following the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, but the news portal in question described the call as a “U-turn”. — Bernama
269f7ed8cffcc395: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) deputy president Datuk Ahmad Najmi Abdul Razak wants Malaysian players to ignore social media messages against the national team.
"There were netizens who supported the national team by saying, don't give up. But there were also netizens who wrote some unpleasant things about the players.
"Writing bad things against the national team on social media is not giving the national players encouragement. The national players have played very hard for the country.
"I have seen them train hard and play really hard for Malaysia. I don't know what is in the fans' hearts to say or write bad things about the national players.
"I told the players not to worry about what people said or wrote. I still thank the hockey fans for supporting the team and for those who hit them.

"I told the players to take it in stride, as their words can encourage them to play much better for the Asian Games. We also want the media to write positive things about the national team," said men's team manager Najmi at a press conference at the National Hockey Stadium in Bukit Jalil on Friday.
Meanwhile, Najmi said MHC have set a top-four target for the national women's team for the Asian Games.

"The national women's team have finished fifth in the last five Asian Games (since 2006 in Doha) and we have faith that national coach C. R. Kumar of India will guide the women's team to reach the semi-finals," he said.

Kumar, who coached the national women's team from 2002 to 2006, introduced a more demanding strength and condition programme to improve power, explosiveness, speed, physicality and ability to compete with bigger Asian teams.

Malaysia women's team are drawn in Group A with defending champion China, South Korea, Kazakhstan, Taiwan and Bangladesh while Group B comprises India, Japan, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia and Uzbekistan.
Kumar said South Korea are also rebuilding their team and they hope to get the better of them to finish top two in their group to reach the semi-finals.
"In preparation for the Asian Games, we played seven matches with Ireland, Wales and Scotland and we are ready for the challenge," he said.
The Asian Games will be Kumar's first national assignment since he was hired as the national coach in April.
The Malaysian women's team's best outing in the Asian Games was bagging bronze in the 1982 in New Delhi.

8a43e6bfb6288508: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) to become part of the national narrative rather than being viewed solely as an issue concerning Sabah and Sarawak.

He said the approach was important to ensure Malaysians understood that the government’s commitment to MA63 formed part of the Madani Government’s national policy and was closely linked to the country’s development, stability and unity.
Anwar said this must be understood and embraced by people in peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak as part of a national policy, commitment and narrative aimed at strengthening the country.
“I have proposed that discussions on MA63 be made part of the national narrative. It is very important because otherwise, it becomes a sectoral issue.
“Every year, we have to hold separate discussions on Sabah and Sarawak. No. This is a national commitment about development, stability, and what we promised when Malaysia was formed.

“This must be firmly established as a national narrative. We need to encourage Malaysians not to speak only about their race, party or group, but to engage in a broader discourse that strengthens the nation,” he told a press conference after chairing the 2026 Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
The Prime Minister said people in peninsular Malaysia should also not view additional allocations or measures implemented under MA63 as merely special considerations for Sabah and Sarawak.

Meanwhile, Abang Johari backed the proposal to place MA63 within a national framework, saying it would align provisions enshrined in the Federal Constitution with efforts to strengthen Malaysia’s unity.
“We want to align what is enshrined in the Constitution with the unity of Malaysia as a united nation, a united Malaysia, as we continue our efforts to develop the country,” he said.
He said the approach was more practical in balancing the interests of the Federal Government, Sabah and Sarawak, including in matters of finance and national development. — Bernama
c804bb5a25bf2560: SHAH ALAM: Selangor has declared Oct 25 a public holiday in conjunction with the 25th anniversary of the reign of the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah.
State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said that as the date falls on a Sunday, the following day, Monday, Oct 26, 2026, will be observed as a replacement public holiday.

"A total of 20 official programmes and events are scheduled to take place from Sept 28 to Nov 1, 2026, as a sign of loyalty, respect and gratitude from the entire administration and people under Sultan Sharafuddin's reign.
"All programmes have been presented to Sultan Sharafuddin, covering social and religious matters, environmental sustainability, infrastructure development and sports," he told a press conference.
Fadzli said the celebrations will be moderate, in line with Sultan Sharafuddin's decree for prudence.
The celebrations will feature three main ceremonies.
"These are a Guard of Honour Inspection with a 21-gun salute, the Proclamation of Titles and Oath-Taking Ceremony, and the presentation of Selangor State Awards," he said.
He said other key events include community programmes such as visits to orphans, the official opening of the Autism Friendly Park, the Kita Run and a Royal Tea Party.
Religious activities include a Yasin recital and prayer session, as well as the Multaqa and Forum Perdana Ehwal Islam.
Heritage and historical documentation programmes include the launch of special envelopes and stamps, a commemorative coin, and a book titled "Menjulang Takhta".
Sports events include the opening of the Selangor Polo and Equestrian Club, the Sultan of Selangor Silver Jubilee Cup Polo Tournament and an Under-15 Football League match.
88640e8ed769d8d0: WASHINGTON, Sept 11 — Hasbro has responded to the US Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) use of Optimus Prime in AI-generated material promoting deportations, saying the character was featured without its permission.

According to Entertainment Weekly, DHS shared several images on its official social media accounts on Wednesday, including one depicting the Transformers character with DHS and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) branding.
Another showed Optimus Prime confronting a bearded Sikh man alongside the phrases “America for Americans”, “Self-deport or find out” and “Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive, Mr Singh”.
The post was removed on Thursday following criticism from Sikh and Indian-American groups, as well as California Governor Gavin Newsom’s office, which accused DHS of targeting the Sikh community.
“Optimus Prime is a beloved character who represents humility, leadership, compassion and justice,” Hasbro said in a statement shared on Instagram.
“Hasbro is aware of the recent posts using his likeness. These posts were done without permission and do not represent the Transformers brand or Hasbro,” it added.
DHS defended the image by saying it depicted Harjinder Singh, an Indian national charged over a Florida highway crash that killed three people in August 2025.
83dd901bf629587a: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s keynote at the party’s general assembly this morning earned praise from Khairy Jamaluddin.

Khairy, an Umno returnee after being sacked three years ago for alleged disciplinary infractions and breaches of party discipline during GE15 – described the speech as crystal clear on Barisan Nasional’s (BN) direction ahead of the coming general election.
“This is the speech of a prime minister in waiting and a speech of a government in waiting,” Khairy told reporters after Zahid’s speech at the 2026 Umno general assembly here.
In his address, Zahid described Umno as a far-sighted party with a long-term vision for Malaysia, rather than one that merely hopes to survive one election after another.
He also called for the GE16 to be held as soon as possible, saying it was time for BN to seek a fresh mandate to lead the country.
Zahid further pledged that Malaysia’s courts and institutions would not be used as political tools should BN return to Putrajaya.

The third day of the assembly was also attended by four PAS leaders, including its vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad, secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, and assistant secretary-general Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman.
487d7bb182170398: VENICE: A chilling new documentary about Israel's AI-powered mass killing of civilians in Gaza from two Oscar-winning Israeli filmmakers received a 25-minute ovation at its premiere at the Venice Film Festival on Thursday.

The audience clapped continuously for Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor after the screening, an AFP reporter witnessed, setting what is thought to be a new record in Venice after a 23-minute ovation for another film about Gaza last year.
In their film "NAZA", Abraham and Szor used conversations with 24 different Israeli military or intelligence whistleblowers who spoke on condition that their identities be protected.
"We are letting the soldiers and the officers speak about what they did," Abraham told AFP.
"The goal was very simple: we wanted to hear in as much detail as possible what the systems of killing in Gaza looked like, how they operated," he said.
The 80-minute film left many audience members stunned, with interviewees describing how they felt like they worked in a killing "factory" or a lethal video game.
"NAZA" draws its name from a euphemism used by Israeli intelligence to indicate the number of civilians that are expected to be killed in an airstrike.

It was described as an "urgent, gut-punch" by film magazine Screen, while The Hollywood Reporter said it inspired "outrage…indignity as well. Most certainly disgust, on a profound level, for the current Israeli regime".
Israel's bombardment of Gaza has left around 73,500 Palestinians dead and 174,500 wounded since October 2023, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures the UN deems reliable.
The pounding of the territory followed an attack on Israel by Hamas militants on Oct 7, 2023, that resulted in the death of 1,219 people, according to an AFP tally based on official figures.
First-person testimony
The men and women featured in "NAZA", with their voices and faces digitally altered, detail an AI-powered system known as "Lavender" that was used to identify people for assassination.
"It was done on a mass scale, like a factory," one says, filmed like all of them at night on a roof terrace with an eerily quiet Tel Aviv as the background.

"Lavender" uses data from the mass surveillance of Gaza, where the entire telecommunications network is monitored by Israel, to identify targets based on their phone calls, movements and interactions.
"The system's parameters are so complex, it's hard to understand," one interviewee, who said he worked on the system, told the filmmakers.
Others describe the systematic destruction of civilian homes, the disregard for war and humanitarian laws, and a "general atmosphere" of "hatred" towards Palestinians.
"It's like a video game because everything is done remotely," one interviewee involved in identifying targets says at one point.
Another describes it as "insanely fun".
Gaza films
The result of a nearly three-year investigation, "NAZA" is the only documentary in competition at this year's Venice Film Festival, which wraps up on Saturday.
Ovations can be easily manipulated and are seen as an imperfect measure of a film, but they do give an indication of the impact on festival-goers and critics.
Along with Palestinian peers Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal, Abraham and Szor won an Oscar in 2025 for their film "No Other Land" about Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank.

Their latest movie has been produced by Britain's Jim Wilson with help from Jonathan Glazer – the team behind Auschwitz-set Oscar winner "The Zone of Interest" – as well as Britain's Guardian newspaper.
The war in Gaza retains broad Israeli public support, but Abraham and Szor said they hoped it would encourage Western nations to drop their backing for Israel and apply pressure through sanctions.
"Those of us inside Israel and Palestine trying to fight for change need it," Abraham told AFP.
"You are weakening the people inside who are supporting human rights and a political solution by refusing to act".
Israel denies deliberately targeting civilians in Gaza, accusing Hamas of hiding among the population of the densely packed and besieged enclave where around two million people lived before the war.

Last year, "The Voice of Hind Rajab", a docu-drama about the killing of a five-year-old Palestinian girl by Israeli forces, picked up second prize at the festival after receiving a 23-minute standing ovation at its premiere.

Increasing numbers of top entertainment figures are openly criticising the Israeli government, as part of a shift in public opinion in Western countries against prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's policies.
Foreign journalists have been prevented from reporting from Gaza since the start of the conflict, except under tightly controlled conditions with the Israeli military.

36567688d2a7be69: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today showed off his Gen Z lingo, urging the younger generation to "slay", "flex" their ideas and bring a "W", or win, to the party.
In an unusually youthful turn of phrase during his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly, Zahid told young members not to keep their ideas to themselves.
"If my young ones have ideas that are 'slay', don't keep them to yourselves. Flex them. Let us see who can really bring a 'W' to Umno. For real, for real," he said.
Zahid then acknowledged that such language was part of how young people communicated today, calling on Umno Youth and Puteri Umno members to engage with them on their terms.
"Do we understand the language of young people? Can we speak like this with them? This is their language now.
"To the Youth and Puteri, get closer to them and engage with them so that they will come to us," he said.

His remarks came as he outlined the "Rumah Bangsa" agenda, which he said was aimed at strengthening Umno from within by providing space for those who had become disillusioned with the party, distanced themselves from it or wanted to contribute again.
Zahid said the "house" would remain open to those who had previously broken ties with the party or built their own political platforms.
"For those who have burned bridges, for those who have built walls of differences, for those who have built new huts for shelter, it does not matter... Come back.
"Bridges can be reconnected. Walls can be torn down. Huts can be left behind.
"This house is big enough to welcome all of you," he said.
Zahid said the party's struggle should unite its members rather than become a platform for rekindling old disputes.
"We gather in this house because of our love for the struggle. And the struggle will never fade.
"Just... do not come back to reignite the flames of conflict," he said.
He also called on young members to make Rumah Bangsa a space for their ideas and aspirations, telling them they had a role in reshaping the party.
"To the young people, make Rumah Bangsa a place for you to create and express yourselves. Father is opening up as much space as possible for you to paint the canvas of Umno's struggle.
"This house is also your house. Come in, open its windows, rearrange its spaces and colour the walls of its struggle with the ideas and dreams of your generation.
"Father only wants to ensure that this house remains a shelter for generations to come," he said.
005a914190dba846: KUALA LUMPUR: Asean and China are seeking to deepen their decade-long health cooperation as the region confronts emerging public health threats, climate change, demographic shifts and rapid technological transformation.

Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the partnership is entering an increasingly consequential chapter, with both sides working towards resilient, inclusive and sustainable health systems capable of responding to present and future challenges.

"Our gathering today comes at a defining moment as we face the rapidly evolving health landscape, shaped by emerging public health threats, climate change, demographic shifts and accelerating technological transformation.

"These challenges remind us that resilient health systems are no longer simply a national priority. They are a shared regional imperative," he said in his opening remarks when chairing the 10th Asean-China Health Ministers' Meeting in conjunction with the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings today.
The meeting was co-chaired with Vice-Minister of China's National Health Commission Dr Liu Jinfeng.

Dzulkefly said discussions at the meeting, themed 'Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future Ready Health Systems', would also contribute to the implementation of the Asean Strategic Health Agenda (ASHA) 2026-2030 and translate common aspirations into practical action.
"The decisions and perspectives we share today have the potential to strengthen the health and resilience of more than two billion people across Asean and China.
"Let us seize this opportunity to build a decade of partnership and look ahead with renewed resolve to deepen our cooperation for the decades to come," he added.

He said the meeting also aims to provide strategic direction in advancing the Asean-China Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on health cooperation, capture collective commitments through a Joint Statement and ensure the partnership delivers tangible benefits to the people.
5284a51f610762a8: TAIPEI: Micron Technology said on Friday its direct labour employees in Taiwan would receive bonuses equaling 35 to 68 months of pay for fiscal 2026, with minimum cash compensation of T$1.7 million (US$53,809.39), after the US chipmaker enjoyed what it described as an extraordinary year.
Micron said the payouts to the employees, including operators, technicians and shift engineers, were its strongest ever and that more than 60,000 employees globally will receive fiscal 2026 rewards.

The announcement comes after unions representing around two-thirds of Micron's workforce in Taiwan signaled widespread support among members for a strike. The unions did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The rewards include a T$1 million (US$31,652.58) cash bonus for Taiwan employees, who joined before August 29, 2025, for fiscal 2026, the US memory maker said.
For entry-level engineers, total rewards average T$3.4 million, including an average of T$2.9 million in cash compensation, with the remainder comprising equity at grant value, the company said.
Every employee will also receive an annual equity grant, Micron said.
Micron employs about 15,000 people in Taiwan, one of its most important manufacturing hubs, and said it has invested more than T$1.6 trillion in the island.
The US memory maker and the Taoyuan union failed to reach an agreement during a mediation meeting last week, with a second round of mediation scheduled.

Micron is looking to avoid being dragged into a crisis similar to what its Korean rival Samsung Electronics faced in May, when a planned 18-day strike by as many as 48,000 union members was called off after last-minute negotiations and a successful deal that created a special bonus pool worth 10.5 per cent of the chip division's operating profit, subject to profitability targets.
Back then the prospect of a stoppage at the world's largest memory-chip maker had raised worries about chip supplies and broader economic fallout in Asia's fourth-largest economy.
Micron's Taiwanese unions previously said profit-sharing arrangements at Samsung and SK Hynix had widened the gap between Micron workers and their South Korean peers.
2a877dec1817a59f: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad says Umno's proposed "Blue Malaysia" agenda broadly aligns with his party's vision for national unity and cooperation.

He said Pas had already established its own platform for unity and development through Wawasan Induk Sejahtera 2051, which shared similarities with the vision outlined by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

"Actually, that is also the agenda we have in Wawasan Induk Sejahtera. It is more or less the same as what is being proposed today as Blue Malaysia," he said after attending the 2026 Umno General Assembly today.
Earlier, Zahid proposed the "Blue Malaysia Agenda" as part of Umno's vision for the country.
He said the agenda aims to create a high-income nation and prosperous society, while ensuring Malaysia is respected globally.
Idris said Pas attended the assembly to strengthen ties between both parties and highlight the importance of cooperation in Malaysia's political landscape.
He said that Umno and Pas remained among the political parties with strong grassroots bases, adding that closer relations could reinforce overall political cooperation.
Idris said grassroots cooperation between both parties was already underway, with members encouraged to build ties and explore joint initiatives ahead of future state and general elections.
He said that the process went beyond top-level political alignment, focusing heavily on solidifying relationships on the ground.
Meanwhile, Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan rejected claims that cooperation between Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional was loose.
"That is wrong. You can see our presence today. Our presence here is clear," Takiyuddin said.

Separately, Nik Mohamad Abduh Nik Abdul Aziz, son of the late Pas spiritual leader Tan Sri Nik Abdul Aziz Nik Mat, said Zahid's speech was "very convincing" and reflected confidence in achieving greater unity among Muslims.
He said he believed Umno appreciated the presence of Pas representatives just as the Islamist party welcomed Umno leaders to its muktamar.

80986257896edecc: KUCHING: The post-mortems on all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday were completed at 7.30pm yesterday.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the cause of death for all five victims was severe burn injuries sustained in the helicopter crash.
"For now, we are awaiting the results of the deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) samples for scientific confirmation," he told Bernama.

On Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, had crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport).

The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
7734e3b4503747d6: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Sabah and Sarawak will get a higher proportion of parliamentary representation under a Cabinet decision in principle to increase the number of seats for the two Borneo states, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
Anwar said the Cabinet had agreed to increase the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak, although the exact number and mechanism had yet to be determined.
He stressed that any increase must also raise the proportion of seats held by the two states to reflect the spirit of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
“An increase in the number of seats can be misleading. An increase does not necessarily mean that the ratio will improve; it could simply mean equalising the numbers.

“So the increase must be accompanied by an increase in the proportion of representation for Sabah and Sarawak,” he said in a press conference after chairing the committee meeting for the implementation of the MA63 with Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg present.
Anwar added that there could also be an increase in seats for peninsular Malaysia.
He said the Cabinet made the decision last Wednesday and the Election Commission had been informed to begin discussions on the mechanism and number of additional seats.
Representatives from the two states would subsequently negotiate with political parties from peninsular Malaysia on the details, Anwar said.

Under the original Malaysia Agreement 1963, when Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak and Malaya formed the Federation, the three territories collectively held one-third of the parliamentary seats to prevent Malaya from unilaterally securing the two-thirds majority required to amend the Federal Constitution.

That proportion was reduced after Singapore left the federation in 1965. Of the 222 parliamentary seats today, Sabah has 25 and Sarawak 31, giving the two states a combined 25 per cent of the total compared with 75 per cent for peninsular Malaysia.
Sabah and Sarawak have been seeking a minimum one-third, or 33 per cent, share of parliamentary representation, which would require about 18 additional seats.

“So now we need to look at the mechanism. The principle is that there must be an increase that raises the proportion of representation. We have agreed to that. But the details and mechanics will be discussed with the Election Commission and the various states and political parties,” Anwar said.
Asked whether the increased representation could be implemented before the next general election, Anwar said he was uncertain whether there would be sufficient time.

“I am not certain whether there will be sufficient time because we have to follow the process. I do not want to interfere with the constitutional process. But the important thing is that the decision has been made and the Election Commission has been informed,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government was expediting the appointment of more Sabah- and Sarawak-born Malaysians to key government positions, another matter he said was recognised under MA63.
He said the first phase had already been implemented, while the second phase would be expedited.
Anwar described MA63 as a national commitment rather than an issue concerning only Sabah and Sarawak.
“I had proposed that discussions on MA63 be made part of the national narrative. This is very important because otherwise it becomes a sectoral matter that we have to discuss separately every year.
“It is a national commitment about development, stability, and the commitments we made at independence, Malaya in 1957 and Malaysia in 1963,” he said.
He said the issue should be viewed as part of efforts to strengthen Malaysia as a whole, rather than through the lens of race, political parties or regional interests.
f1570a7de8dfee4d: ARAU: The Raja of Perlis Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail granted an audience to deputy army chief Lieutenant General Datuk Mohamad Suria Mohamad Saad at the Balai Mengadap Hijau, Istana Arau yesterday.

675d888675896703: KINSHASA: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has spread to the northwestern province of Sud-Ubangi after a case was confirmed, local authorities said on Thursday, reported Xinhua.

Sud-Ubangi’s acting governor Jean-Rene Galekwa Vundawe said in a statement that laboratory tests confirmed Bundibugyo ebolavirus in a sample, prompting authorities to declare an outbreak in the province.
Sud-Ubangi does not border any of the six provinces where confirmed Ebola cases had previously been reported, namely Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo and Bas-Uele.
Authorities have not disclosed the source of the infection or any known epidemiological link to the existing outbreak.
Galekwa said authorities will continue to strengthen surveillance, ensure treatment of patients and work to interrupt chains of transmission.
According to the latest official figures, the DRC had recorded 6,843 confirmed Ebola cases as of Sept 8, including 3,310 deaths and 1,611 recoveries, with the case fatality rate standing at 48.4%.
The current outbreak, declared in May, has become the country's largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic on record and the second-largest globally, behind the 2014-2016 epidemic in West Africa.
39a7f5a886d63be3: BUDAPEST: Jamaican sprint legend Usain Bolt claimed 19 global titles in a storied career, but he wishes the kind of prize money on offer at the Ultimate Championship from Friday had been available when he was competing.

Bolt got rich from appearance fees and endorsements off the track rather than prize money as he claimed treble sprint golds at the 2008, 2012 and 2016 Olympics, also picking up two 4x100m sprint titles.
At the world championships, the now 40-year-old won consecutive 100m, 200m and 4X100m relay golds medals from 2009-15, with the exception of 2011 when he false-started.

Importantly, the Jamaican, still the world record holder in the 100 and 200m, built up an off-track persona that combined a towering presence alongside his achievements that always ensured he was in high demand.
Bolt brought down the curtain on his glittering career at the 2017 world championships in London and the gaping hole he left in track and field has never quite been filled.

But he has been brought on board as an ambassador for the inaugural Ultimate Championship in Budapest, a three-day biennial competition launched by World Athletics president Sebastian Coe as a season-ender for a year without a world championships or Olympic Games.

"I was happy when Seb explained to me that this is what we're doing. It was a no brainer to be a part of it," Bolt said of the Ultimate, with 28 disciplines delivered in a fast-paced, made-for-television format.
"I'm sad this is happening now! But I guess that's just one of those things. I'm here to enjoy it and to promote it and just to let the world know that track and field is here to stay.
"We're going to continue pushing and continue growing the sport itself to bigger and better things. I'm happy to be a part of this and it's going to be great."
The Ultimate features an unprecedented $10 million prize money pot, with individual event winners collecting $150,000.
Should a sprinter win the 100m, 200m and relay in Budapest, it would make for an impressive payday.
"I was having a conversation with Asafa before I came here," Bolt said of former Jamaican teammate Asafa Powell.
"We were actually talking about that same thing. I mean, jeez, we missed out on this cash prize!"
Bolt added: "I won a few championships and it still does not add up to all the cash.
"So, it's big. I think it's good for the sport and it incentivises athletes to come out here and do the best, to show up and to be ready.
"This is a job for us. This is what we do. So, it's sad I missed out on it but I'm happy for the athletes."
Coe's ground-breaking move to award prize money to track and field gold medallists at the 2024 Paris Olympics ruffled some feathers.
While the unilateral decision sparked a backlash from within the International Olympic Committee, Bolt argued that it was essential.
"We put such big weight on the Olympics," he said. "I fully agree that athletes should be compensated for what they do.
"It's work. Yes, you're competing for your country, but you're putting your body on the line."
Turning to the Ultimate, Bolt said he would have loved to compete.
"If you follow my career you know that's what I'm about," he said.
"For me, I'm about competing against the best. I always show up when it matters.
"I'm excited because with the Ultimate Championship, you know that the 16 people that show up are the best in the world no matter what event they're doing.

"I live for this moment, I live for competition, it's something that I always strive for, so definitely it will be something that I look at as big as an Olympics as a world championships, for sure." - AFP

03d5c59823a09eba: KUALA LUMPUR: Terengganu coach Nafuzi Zain has warned his players against complacency despite their morale-boosting 3-2 win over Brunei's DPMM in the FA Cup ahead of their Super League clash against Star City on Saturday.
The Turtles ended a two-match winless run in the league with the victory over the Brunei side in the first leg of the FA Cup first round on Wednesday.
However, Nafuzi knows his players cannot afford to carry the wrong mentality into the fourth league match at the Tuanku Syed Putra Stadium in Kangar.
The former international stressed that every match presents a different challenge, particularly when playing away from home.
"The win against the Brunei club certainly lifted the players' morale after we failed to collect maximum points in our last two league matches.
"But I have reminded the players not to be too comfortable. They must remain focused for the full 90 minutes because every match is different, especially when playing away.
"I believe in the players' ability. Most importantly, they must take their chances and avoid simple mistakes that could prove costly.
"At the same time, they need to improve their performance and raise the quality of their game by being more organised," said Nafuzi, the former national Under-23 coach.
Terengganu are seventh in the standings with four points after three matches, having opened their campaign with a 3-0 win over Melaka before losing 3-0 to Selangor and drawing 0-0 with Penang.
Nafuzi is also hoping two of his foreign players, Victor Ruiz and Gervane Kastaneer, will recover from minor injuries in time for the match against Mehmet Durakovic's men.
He said both players were important to the team but would only be considered after their fitness was assessed.

"They are important to the team, but we will assess their condition first before deciding whether they can start. If they are still unavailable, we have several players who can fill their roles, as they did against DPMM.
"We don't want to take any risks, especially with the long journey and short recovery period. But we still want to make sure the team is in the best possible condition," he said.
437a71da075ede70: KUALA LUMPUR: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has completed the acquisition of the remaining 30.95 per cent stake in Maybank Ageas Holdings Bhd.
This gives the banking group full ownership of the holding company for its Etiqa insurance and takaful business in Malaysia and Singapore.
The transaction follows Maybank's share purchase agreement with Ageas Insurance International NV on Sept 8 and regulatory approval from Bank Negara Malaysia received on Sept 1.
With the completion, Maybank Ageas becomes a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank.

Maybank president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli said the acquisition marks a significant milestone as the group seeks to strengthen Etiqa's position as a national insurance and takaful champion, while expanding its footprint across Southeast Asia.
He said the move also supports Maybank's
ROAR30 strategy to build a stronger regional franchise and establish a global takaful powerhouse.

"With Maybank Ageas being a wholly owned subsidiary of Maybank, it strengthens Etiqa's position as a national insurance and takaful champion, driving deeper penetration of Maybank's customer base," said Khairussaleh.
Full ownership is expected to give Maybank greater flexibility to integrate its banking, wealth and protection offerings, particularly across its regional customer base.
Khairussaleh said Maybank intends to unlock further value through cross-selling and more integrated, personalised financial solutions.

The acquisition should also support more effective capital management within Maybank Ageas and at the wider Maybank group level, potentially improving the insurance business's efficiency and resilience.
Etiqa will continue to operate as one of Maybank's key brands, offering life and general conventional insurance alongside family and general takaful products through multiple distribution channels.
"The Etiqa brand remains a strong and well-established insurance and takaful franchise, and it will continue to be positioned as one of Maybank's flagship brands," said Khairussaleh.
With Maybank's extensive customer base and distribution network behind it, Etiqa is expected to pursue growth opportunities as demand rises for more integrated and personalised protection solutions.
Maybank also acknowledged Ageas' contribution to the development of the Etiqa franchise over the past 25 years.
f2b4bf5c5fabad6a: KOTA KINABALU: A review of the Special Grant under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution was among four key issues discussed at the first 2026 meeting of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63), chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today.

Anwar said the other matters discussed were strengthening border security, increasing posts and the 'Borneonisation' of the federal public service, and increasing the number of parliamentary seats in Sabah and Sarawak.

He said the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) is not merely a historical record or a document commemorated each year, but a national trust and commitment that must be fulfilled with sincerity, fairness and full responsibility.

"What has been agreed upon must be implemented, while matters that remain unresolved must continue to be negotiated with wisdom, sincerity and a spirit of consensus," he said in a post on his Facebook page.

bf3db2aebc6d6a69: KUALA LUMPUR: Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd is maintaining its end-2026 FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) target at 1,770 points, seeing stronger earnings visibility from power and grid investments than the semiconductor cycle.
The research house said the benchmark index had traded largely between 1,700 and 1,740 points since late August, slipping below 1,710 in the first week of September.
Foreign investors turned net sellers of about RM2 billion in August, reversing the buying trend in July, while local retail investors remained net buyers for a fourth consecutive month.
"The market is being held up by domestic money, that largely follows earnings visibility rather than announcements.

"We are keeping our 1,770 target because recent results season depicted growth remains intact with utilities being one of the contributors and they sit in the grid, not in the chip cycle," Rakuten head of research Kenny Yee said in a statement.
Against this backdrop, Rakuten sees Malaysia's ongoing investment in power infrastructure as a key earnings catalyst into year-end and beyond.
Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) grid capital expenditure programme is expected to rise to RM43 billion between 2025 and 2027, compared with RM21 billion spent between 2022 and 2024.
Further investment is expected through 2030 as the national grid is upgraded to support renewable energy, battery storage and rising electricity demand, including from data centres.
The government has also identified energy transition as one of five priority sectors for the 2027 Budget, alongside semiconductors, the digital economy, artificial intelligence and Islamic finance.
Yee said the longer duration of grid investment provided greater earnings visibility than semiconductor orders, which can change within a quarter.
"A grid programme running to 2030 cannot. The money is committed and the work is sequenced.
"Earnings then show up within the companies involved, usually within the utility and construction segments," he said.

The opportunity extends beyond traditional renewable energy plays, with grid expansion requiring sustained investment in transmission, substations, electrical systems and related engineering works, Rakuten said.
It identified TNB, Kee Ming Group Bhd and Gamuda Bhd as its preferred beneficiaries of the theme.

TNB, with a target price of RM17, owns and operates Malaysia's electricity transmission and distribution network and is positioned to benefit directly from continued grid investment and rising electricity demand.
Growing data centre capacity provides an additional long-term demand driver, while the stock offers an estimated dividend yield of about 3.5 per cent.
Kee Ming Group, with a target price of RM1.30, provides mechanical and electrical engineering services and has an unbilled order book of about RM151.9 million.
Its strategic shareholder relationship with Solarvest Holdings Bhd also provides exposure to Malaysia's developing energy infrastructure.
Gamuda, with a target price of RM5.30, has an outstanding order book of RM55.4 billion, providing multi-year earnings visibility across its domestic infrastructure and overseas operations.
"We would rather own the people building the network than guess which technology wins on top of it," Yee said.
He said the 1,770-point KLCI target also hinged on the 2027 Budget, which will be tabled on Oct 9, confirming rather than materially deferring planned energy-transition spending.

"If the budget pushes energy-transition spending into the back half of the plan period, or the grid allocation comes in materially below what has been signalled, we would revisit the number," he said.

Rakuten also highlighted risks from weaker-than-expected budget allocations, delays in major infrastructure tenders and project execution, continued foreign fund outflows and volatility in global interest rates.
It said the run-up to the 2027 Budget would be less about chasing the latest market headline and more about identifying sectors where earnings are underpinned by committed investment programmes.

9ba19dbeed34880e: BERLIN: The United States breezed into the semi-finals of the Women's Basketball World Cup with a 108-56 win against Hungary on Thursday and will face Spain for a place in the final.

Napheesa Collier top-scored with 19 points while Caitlin Clark delivered nine assists and added 10 points in a dominant quarter-final performance in Berlin from the nation seeking a fifth consecutive title.

The Americans and their roster packed with WNBA stars will face Spain in the semi-finals on Saturday and they remain on course to play the team they beat in the 2024 Olympic final, France, in the gold medal game.
Having survived a scare from Italy, who pushed them all the way in their second pool game before the Americans won 55-52, the USA have gone from strength to strength in the tournament in Germany.
On Thursday they raced into a 36-12 lead in the first quarter, effectively ending the game as a contest.
Spain defeated Australia 89-66 to earn the chance to meet the Americans.
France were convincing 90-61 winners against China to secure their semi-final berth against host nation Germany.
WNBA star Xu Han led all scorers with 21 points, but her contribution was not enough for the Chinese to contend with the all-round performance of the French.
Janelle Salaun and Marine Johannes both scored 15 points for France and US-born Gabby Williams added 14 points.
Zhang Ziyu, China's towering 2.23 metre (7ft 4in) teenage centre, played 18 minutes and scored seven points, but at the age of 19 she has shown in this tournament that she has a bright future.
Roared on by the home crowd, the Germans defeated Belgium 93-74 despite a 29-point performance from Belgian power forward Emma Meesseman. - AFP
8cb4ccef44cfaac6: MADRID: Two-time world champion Fernando Alonso teased reporters on the eve of his home Spanish Grand Prix on Thursday when asked if he had made a long-awaited decision on his future in Formula One.

After a disappointing season to date with Aston Martin in the new hybrid-era cars introduced this year, it was widely expected that Alonso would make an announcement ahead of the first race at the new Madring circuit.
But asked if a decision was due, he simply replied: "Not soon."
And when asked why he was continuing to delay, he added: "Because I think it's nice."

The 45-year-old preferred to remain evasive and ironic on the subject of whether Aston Martin were pressing him to make a decision, but made clear he was aware of other drivers speaking to team owner Lawrence Stroll about a possible vacant seat.
To explain his position, he said he was hoping that changes to this year's rules would make racing more enjoyable and satisfying next year.
"Next year, there is a step, in the right direction, hopefully," he added.
Alonso also revealed he was considering various options, including a possible switch to a different role with the team. - AFP
e6ba7bd23eb01562: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today expressed disappointment over the postponement of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency application, but said the party continues to hope for a favourable outcome.
Zahid said Umno respected the decision and would continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers while appealing to His Majesty the King to use his wisdom in deciding Najib’s application.
“We are saddened by the decision. Nevertheless, we continue to express our deepest respect to His Majesty the King, and we appeal to His Majesty to use all his wisdom to make the best decision.

“We continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers. We continue to support the Rulers, and we hope that something favourable will be granted to Datuk Seri Najib Abdul Razak,” he told reporters after delivering his policy speech at Umno’s general assembly here.
The Prime Minister’s Department today said Najib’s clemency application had been deferred to a future sitting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board.
The department – which covers Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya – said the board held its 63rd meeting this morning with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim consenting to the postponement.
Earlier this morning Zahid expressed hope for the “best” news for Najib during his policy speech at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
Umno delegates greeted Najib’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, enthusiastically with applause after Zahid asked her to stand for a moment during his speech.

Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison and a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on August 23, 2022.
In 2024, the Federal Territories Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
Najib and his lawyers subsequently argued that the partial pardon included a royal addendum allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, and sued to have it enforced.
On December 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest.
Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.
a94dd4c64c46a3bf: KUCHING: Proses bedah siasat kesemua lima mangsa nahas helikopter Perkhidmatan Doktor Udara (FDS) di Long Lellang, pada Selasa lepas selesai pada 7.30 malam tadi.

Pesuruhjaya Polis Sarawak, Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, berkata bedah siasat yang dijalankan di Jabatan Forensik Hospital Miri mendapati punca kematian kesemua mangsa adalah disebabkan kecederaan melecur teruk.

Pada Selasa, helikopter BO-105 yang membawa lima individu termasuk juruterbang, terhempas berdekatan Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport).

Mangsa yang terkorban ialah juruterbang Kapten Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, pegawai perubatan Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, pembantu perubatan Alexson Adit Henry, 31, serta dua jururawat, Debra Moset, 40, dan Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
78fdca0de0d5e0c4: MADRID: Formula One drivers are expecting a weekend of crashes and chaos at the new Circuito de Madring as it hosts the Spanish Grand Prix for the first time.
"I'll put my money on a red flag," said Alpine's Pierre Gasly, who won his maiden pole position at last weekend's Italian Grand Prix at Monza. "That's for sure."
Like most drivers, the Frenchman took a considered stroll on Thursday around the 5.416-km hybrid track built at a cost of more than €83 million.

His team-mate Franco Colapinto said he was looking forward to trying it in his car in Friday's practice, but warned that "this track is going to be extremely difficult for all the drivers – in the simulator, putting together one complete lap could take me hours."
He added: "It has a bit of everything. If you took all you find at the 24 races on the calendar and mixed it up, you'd probably get something like this."
Cadillac's Sergio Perez, a 36-year-old veteran of 294 Grands Prix, said: "It's scary!
"It reminds me of Jeddah – a good, fast and proper track. I'm really happy to be here, and I think the atmosphere here is going to be one of the best."
The Mexican said he expected it to be an unforgiving circuit with low grip offering no room for error.

The circuit hosted a filming day with Ferrari in action on a very hot day in July, before the building work was completed, and held a Formula Three event in August that saw three cars wrecked and 19 red flag interruptions. - AFP
40a3b54304a973cf: KUALA LUMPUR: The "Blue Malaysia" agenda should strengthen Barisan Nasional through closer ties and greater understanding among all communities, including its partners in Sabah and Sarawak, said Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said the agenda called for a stronger and deeper understanding within BN that recognised the cultural, religious, ethnic and lifestyle differences among the communities it represented.

"Blue Malaysia, as I understand it, is about changing and rethinking Barisan Nasional, and strengthening it through closer and better understanding that carries greater value and involves other communities.

"This includes the Chinese, Indian and other communities, as well as our component parties in Sabah and Sarawak," he told reporters after attending the opening of the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Johari said the agenda was intended to make BN more inclusive while preserving the identities and distinct characteristics of its component parties.
He said any future political cooperation should be based on mutual acceptance, with each party retaining its own culture, ideology and identity.
"If anyone wants to join together, there must be a fundamental basis that we can accept one another. Each party's culture, ideology and identity cannot be taken away," he said.
Johari said the approach was important as BN continued to strengthen itself and respond to changing expectations among voters.

Meanwhile, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's presidential policy speech had clearly set out the party's direction and presented a broader proposition for the country.
"Besides setting out Umno's position and direction, at least this is an offer from Umno to the country for consideration.
"We are very clear about what we want to do and believe the people will give due consideration to the proposals and plans of Umno and Barisan Nasional," he said.
Earlier, Zahid, in his policy speech, proposed the "Blue Malaysia Agenda" as part of the party's vision for the country ahead of the centenary of independence.
Zahid said the agenda would be pursued if Umno, Barisan Nasional and their political allies returned to Putrajaya.
b751ffa31e5c26e1: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa today denied making a U-turn on the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission, saying she had remained committed to the initiative since 2023.

She said a report by a health portal yesterday, which claimed she had reversed her stance, was inaccurate and did not reflect the full context, stressing that efforts on the matter had continued throughout her tenure at the Health Ministry (MoH).

In a statement, Dr Zaliha said that as early as February 2023, she had publicly stated that the proposal to establish the commission was among the key matters being considered in the final draft of the Health White Paper.

"In fact, in April 2023, the same news portal reported on my meeting with representatives of Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK), where the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission and a Health Reform Commission was discussed within the framework of the White Paper," she said.

On her parliamentary reply on June 15, 2023, which she said had often been misinterpreted, Dr Zaliha explained that it was a clarification on the scope of authority of a Service Commission under Article 144 of the Federal Constitution.

She said the functions of a Service Commission cover appointments, confirmation of service, promotions, transfers and disciplinary action, but establishing such a commission does not give it the power to create new posts or formulate remuneration systems, including setting more competitive emolument rates.

"I also explained that establishing a new Service Commission would involve a complex process, including the need to amend the Federal Constitution and secure a two-thirds majority in both the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara.

"That explanation was about the structure, jurisdiction and limitations of the model available at the time, and was not an outright rejection of the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission," she said.

Dr Zaliha cited records after the July 2023 parliamentary session showing that she had publicly confirmed the government's intention to establish the commission and was assessing the best model for it.

She said the commitment was followed by the establishment of a Technical Working Group by the MOH in October 2023 to identify the best methods and mechanisms for setting up the Health Service Commission.

Dr Zaliha reiterated that her position on the welfare of healthcare workers had remained unchanged, stressing that any reform of the healthcare service system, including the establishment of the commission, must be implemented urgently and backed by an authority capable of resolving the crises faced by healthcare personnel.

According to media reports yesterday, Dr Zaliha called for the government to expedite the establishment of the commission following the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, but the news portal in question described the call as a 'U-turn'.
76d14a0b0546a21c: DUBLIN: Rory McIlroy battled against fierce winds to remain in contention at the Irish Open on Thursday with a one under par opening round to sit four shots behind leader Joaquin Niemann.
US President Donald Trump is set to jet in to attend the event over the weekend, which is being held at his resort in the County Clare village of Doonbeg.
Northern Irishman McIlroy is defending his title and aiming to win for the first time since collecting a second green jacket at the Masters in April.
A double bogey six at the 13th set the world number two back, but those were the only dropped shots of his round, which was disrupted by the blustery conditions leading to a glacial pace of play.
"I hung in there, shot under par, and at least don't feel like I'm out of the tournament. A good day tomorrow gets me right back in it," said the six-time major champion.
"There were a couple of things that were tough today. Obviously the wind and the strength of the wind was one thing, and then the pace of play."
"This course isn't conducive to sort of letting you get in a flow. Especially the first two days with so many people in the field, there is a lot of stopping and starting."
Niemann made four birdies in a row from the 14th to forge ahead.
"It's a really tricky course and a really fun golf course to play with, especially with the Irish weather," said the Chilean. "(I'm) getting used to this weather and the rain, so it was fun."
Delays caused by the conditions meant that some players will have to return early on day two to complete their opening rounds.
Home favourite Shane Lowry is among a five-strong group, two shots behind Niemann after a 67.
Adrian Meronk, Maximilian Steinlechner and Renato Paratore were also at three under when bad light brought their opening day to an end without completing their rounds.
Jon Rahm was level par on a rare appearance back on the DP World Tour as speculation surrounds his future after LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy in the US. - AFP
ec810e48d3f78dd6: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno's political recovery will depend on whether its leaders at all levels can maintain the momentum and act on the message delivered by party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

Former Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Hishammuddin Hussein said the party's experience over the past eight years showed that political fortunes could change, with Umno moving from a period of decline to one of recovery.
"I think the speech touched on the party's journey over the past eight years. The lessons from those eight years show that in politics there are cycles.
"There are times when we rise and times when we fall. When we rise, we are praised and supported.

"But when we fell over the past eight years, we were criticised, attacked and subjected to allegations," he said after Zahid delivered his presidential policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly today.
Hishammuddin said Umno was now showing signs of recovery, but it was up to the current leadership to ensure the momentum continued.

8472dee0a0427a14: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today vowed that Malaysia’s courts and institutions would not be used as political tools if Barisan Nasional (BN) returns to Putrajaya.

2f13455ea7eaebd5: SINGAPORE: Vessel transits at the Strait of Hormuz fell to seven on Thursday from 11 the previous day, preliminary ship-tracking data showed on Friday, well below the 10-day average of 15.
Of the seven vessels, two Panamax ships exited the strait, one carrying fertiliser and the other sailing in ballast, according to data from ship tracker Kpler as of 0306 GMT.

Five vessels entered the strait, including a Panamax vessel carrying dry bulk cargo, a Handysize vessel laden with steel, a Handysize vessel carrying grains, a medium-range tanker loaded with dirty petroleum products, and a Supramax vessel carrying dry bulk cargo.
The figures exclude any vessels that might have crossed the strait with their Automatic Identification System transponders turned off to avoid detection.

Meanwhile, two ballast QatarEnergy-linked vessels, the Al Ghashamiya and the Al Daayen, appeared inside the Strait of Hormuz this week on Sept 9 and 6, respectively, after last being seen outside the waterway on Sept 6 and 3.

Another QatarEnergy-controlled vessel, Al Marrouna, also exited the Strait of Hormuz this week, delivering a cargo from Ras Laffan to Pakistan on Sept 10. The voyage marked the first known LNG shipment aboard a Qatar-linked tanker since late July, when Al Areesh carried a cargo from Ras Laffan also to Pakistan.
QatarEnergy did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside business hours.

Before the Iran war started on Feb 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large, commercial vessels per day, including tankers, gas carriers, bulkers and container vessels, accounting for some 20% of the world’s daily crude oil and liquefied natural gas supply.
A US blockade of Iran-related shipping has halted Iranian crude oil exports since it was reimposed in mid-July.
In the Red Sea, Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha on Thursday and advanced down the Red Sea coast to strategic islands, military sources said.
In the Bab el-Mandeb strait on Thursday, 26 commodity vessels travelled through, tracking data showed. Of these, 10 vessels entered and 16 exited.
This compares with an average of around 27 ships over the last 10 days.
e4215df585200431: SYDNEY: A shortage of air traffic controllers caused flight cancellations and major delays at Sydney Airport on Friday morning, the federal agency responsible for managing Australia's air traffic said.
Airservices Australia said it imposed measures to manage air traffic flows "to safely manage aviation demand" because of the staffing shortage.
That led to around 14 cancellations of inbound flights, and delays of more than one hour.
The disruption is the latest to hit the nation's busiest airport as Airservices Australia grapples with staff shortages, and comes amid probes into several recent near-misses at the airport.

"Last night, at relatively short notice, we had some unplanned absenteeism, which we weren't able to recover from," Airservices Australia deputy chief executive Peter Curran told a Senate committee examining the aviation sector on Friday.
"We're one down in the tower this morning and that led to some significant delays," he said.
The air traffic measures were lifted at 8.15am after conditions improved. Some minor delays continued for the rest of the morning, with flights back on schedule in the afternoon.
Airservices was working with airlines to reduce delays and the impact on passenger travel as much as possible, a spokesman said by email.
Of the 49 controllers employed in Sydney, 41 are needed to be operational.
"Eight have been unavailable due to long-term absences, leaving little room to absorb unexpected shortages," Curran said.
"We've had some staffing challenges in the last number of weeks since July ... and we have some moments where that can become somewhat acute. Today's an example of that," he said.
The agency said it was taking steps to recruit more air traffic controllers and make it easier to call on additional staff when needed.

Last week, a Reuters report — citing internal records and a call recording — said several air traffic controllers on duty when two Qantas aircraft nearly collided at Sydney Airport in July had been flagged as facing a high risk of fatigue.
One shift manager reportedly described the staffing situation as "a bit insane".
That incident was the first of six near-misses at Sydney Airport in the space of about a month, prompting further scrutiny of air traffic control staffing amid global shortages.
The Australian Transport Safety Bureau is investigating the close calls to determine whether they shared common safety issues or contributing factors.

1fc4b8d3232ec86e: PETALING JAYA: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim berkata Perlembagaan akan dipinda bagi membuka ruang penambahan kerusi Parlimen Sabah dan Sarawak sejajar Perjanjian Malaysia 1963 (MA63).
Katanya, berkata penambahan itu perlu memastikan nisbah perwakilan Sabah dan Sarawak menjadi lebih tinggi, berbanding ketika ini.

"Beberapa keputusan yang biasa kita percepatkan, tetapi yang agak utama adalah keputusan untuk meminda Perlembagaan bagi membolehkan penyertaan Ahli-ahli Parlimen Sabah dan Sarawak lebih daripada sepertimana yang dijanjikan dalam MA63.

"Penambahan itu mesti juga melibatkan ratio Sabah-Sarawak itu lebih tinggi. Yang ini kena faham, penambahan Ahli Parlimen itu wewenang Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya (SPR)," katanya menurut Sinar Harian, di Kota Kinabalu.
Anwar berkata demikian pada sidang akhbar selepas mempengerusikan Mesyuarat Majlis Tindakan Pelaksanaan MA63 (MTPMA63) 2026.
Mesyuarat tersebut turut dihadiri Ketua Menteri Sabah Hajiji Noor, Premier Sarawak Abang Johari Openg, dan Menteri di Jabatan Perdana Menteri (Sabah dan Sarawak) Mustapha Sakmud.
Ketika ini, Sabah mempunyai 25 kawasan Parlimen, manakala Sarawak, 31.

Katanya, kemungkinan berlaku penambahan kerusi di Semenanjung juga tidak boleh diketepikan, namun ia tidak boleh menjejaskan prinsip nisbah perwakilan Sabah dan Sarawak perlu ditingkatkan daripada kedudukan sekarang.
Beliau merujuk kedudukan ketika pembentukan Malaysia pada 1963 yang menyaksikan Singapura, Sabah, dan Sarawak secara keseluruhannya mempunyai satu pertiga daripada perwakilan.

"Maknanya, mungkin ada penambahan juga dari Semenanjung, penambahan dari Sabah dan Sarawak, tetapi penambahan ini tidak boleh menjejaskan prinsip ratio perwakilan Sabah dan Sarawak itu harus lebih tinggi daripada yang ada sekarang.
"Walaupun dalam Perjanjian MA63 itu dengan penyertaan Singapura, dia satu pertiga daripada Singapura, Sabah, Sarawak. Sekarang ini tentunya kurang."
Anwar berkata, wakil Sabah dan Sarawak seterusnya akan mengadakan rundingan bersama parti di Semenanjung berhubung perkara itu.

Katanya, prinsip penambahan penyertaan Ahli Parlimen Sabah dan Sarawak telah dipersetujui lebih awal oleh Jemaah Menteri sebelum diluluskan pada mesyuarat Kabinet dengan mengambil kira peningkatan nisbah perwakilan kedua-dua wilayah.

"Penambahan itu boleh jadi mengelirukan, tambah tak bermakna dia mungkin hanya 'equalize' sepertimana yang ada. Jadi, penambahan dengan peningkatan ratio penyertaan Sabah dan Sarawak. Itu yang pertama yang penting," katanya.
0c61158509a61813: SINGAPORE, Sept 11 — A ship crew member hid an African elephant tusk inside a modified thermos flask in an attempt to smuggle it into Singapore, despite knowing that possessing ivory without a permit was illegal, The Straits Times reported.
The 30-year-old Indonesian man, Hafiludin, who goes by one name, was sentenced to eight weeks’ jail on Sept 10 for attempting to smuggle the tusk into the country.

National Parks Board (NParks) prosecutor Lim Chong Hui told the court that Hafiludin bought the tusk for US$150 (S$190) from a travelling merchant while his ship was docked in Lagos, Nigeria, in December 2025.
The tusk was a specimen regulated under the Endangered Species (Import and Export) Act, and Hafiludin did not have the required permits or licences to import it into Singapore, the prosecutor said.
According to the report, aware of Singapore’s laws, Hafiludin decided to conceal the tusk inside a thermos flask, which he sawed open to accommodate the item.
The tusk was about 27cm long and weighed around 550g. He then placed the flask inside his luggage.
The ship entered Singapore’s waters on Aug 8, its last port of call before returning to Indonesia.
Hafiludin disembarked with his luggage the following day at about 12.15pm through the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority’s (ICA) Keppel entrance crew office.
His luggage was subjected to a routine X-ray scan as part of security screening, which led to the discovery of the tusk inside the flask.

Hafiludin initially claimed the tusk was a “cigar-shaped apparatus” made of plastic and used for smoking. The case was subsequently referred to NParks and he was later charged in court, The Straits Time reported.
