722850eb9d319185: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — A document examiner stood by her findings on writings linked to Zara Qairina Mahathir, telling an inquest that the testimony of another forensic handwriting expert had not changed any of her conclusions.
Recalled witness Nurul Atiqah Mohd Noh said Dr Linthini Gannetion’s testimony had not altered any of her findings after she considered the expert’s evidence.
Nurul, the second deponent, was questioned by Deputy Public Prosecutor Dana Arabi Wazani during the inquest into the death of the 13-year-old student before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan on Thursday.
Dana: Overall, after considering Dr Linthini’s testimony, is there anything in her testimony that caused you to change any of the conclusions contained in Exhibit I-31?
Nurul: No.

Dana: Dr Linthini also stated that in Y4B, part of the word “challenge” (“hallenge”) was written in pencil and the word “tauddin” in “Retauddin” may have been added later with a different pen, and that Y13A contained erased writing, including the phrase “Jala imut”. You concluded that Y4 and Y13 were written by the exemplar writer.

If there are scribbles, minor amendments or the use of different writing instruments on a small portion of an entry, in your opinion, does that alter the overall conclusion that the entry was written by Zara?
Nurul: No.

Dana: Dr Linthini emphasised that almost all the sheets from Y1 to Y15 were dated, except Y8B and Y13B, and described this as inconsistent with Zara’s habit of not always recording dates in her journal. In your opinion, is the frequency or pattern of writing dates a scientific criterion in forensic document examination for determining the writer or the existence of interference? Does the habit of writing dates not vary according to the type of entry, such as a daily journal entry compared with an entry addressed to someone, or according to the circumstances in which it was written?
Nurul: The frequency or pattern of writing dates is a characteristic that can be observed, but it is not the only characteristic to prove the identity of a writer.

Nurul was also asked about differences between her findings and those of Dr Linthini Gannetion, a certified handwriting expert who was previously called by Zara’s mother to testify on the examination of the questioned writings.

Dana: Dr Linthini stated that she used the “ACEV” method, namely Analysis, Comparison, Evaluation and Verification. Based on your understanding, what is done under this method, and is it essentially the same as the comparison method used by the Chemistry Department?
Nurul: Based on my understanding, this method is the same.

Dana: In your opinion, are the results of a handwriting examination determined solely by the use of instruments such as Video Spectral Comparator (VSC) or do they depend on the examiner’s skills in identifying, assessing and weighing the characteristics of handwriting?
Nurul: The use of instruments such as VSC is to assist the examination. A comprehensive examination depends on the skills of the document examiner.

Dana: Dr Linthini emphasised that the handwriting of a growing adolescent is volatile and can change within a short period, hence the most reliable comparison is with the most contemporary samples. Do you agree that a person’s handwriting can change over time?
Nurul: Agree.

Dana: If an adolescent’s handwriting is indeed volatile and changes over time, in your opinion, does every small difference in handwriting characteristics at a particular time necessarily indicate a different writer?
Nurul: Not necessarily.

Dana: Dr Linthini, in paragraph 25 of her witness statement, stated that she could not reach any conclusion regarding the writer of Y1A, Y1B, Y2A, Y2B, Y3A, Y3B, Y4A, Y4B, Y5A, Y5B, Y6A, Y6B, Y7A, Y7B, Y8A, Y9A, Y9B and Y10A, among others, due to the absence of contemporary handwriting samples for the period from November 2024 to January 2025.
In your opinion, does the opinion that “no conclusion can be made” mean that the writings were not written by the late Zara Qairina?
Nurul: No.
Dana: Does the opinion that “no conclusion can be made” mean that the writings were written by someone else?
Nurul: No.
Dana: In your previous testimony, you also stated that “Y1” to “Y7” and “Y9” to “Y15” were written by the same person. Is that correct?
Nurul: Correct.
Dana: Please refer to paragraph 21(i) of your second report. Your conclusion was that the writings in W1, W2, W3 and Y1-Y15 were written by the exemplar writer, Zara Qairina Binti Mahathir, correct?
Nurul: Correct.

Dana: Dr Linthini stated that in W2, pages 45, 49 to 51, 58, 59, 61 and 62 contained writings by other individuals besides the late Zara, and she concluded that other people may have had access to W2.
After your comprehensive examination of W2, did you find any pages or portions of W2 that were not written by the exemplar writer?
Nurul: There are writings with slightly different characteristics, but I cannot give an opinion on the writer because there are only a few characters.

Dana: If most of the entries in a journal were written by its owner but there were several lines or entries written by another person, in your opinion, does that necessarily mean that the main entries in the journal were not written by its owner?
Nurul: No.

Dana: Dr Linthini agreed that pages 2, 7 to 14, 25 to 37, 46, 58 to 64, 73 to 84 and 86 to 89 of W3 were not written by the late Zara. So far, are Dr Linthini’s findings consistent with your findings?
Nurul: Yes, consistent.

Dana: In your opinion, does the absence of contemporary samples automatically prevent an examiner from reaching any conclusion, or does it depend on the quality, quantity and consistency of the characteristics of similarities found in the material examined?
Nurul: It depends on the results of the examination, whether similarities or differences are found.

Dana: Based solely on presumptive observations and without confirmatory tests such as ESDA or ink and paper analysis, in your opinion, can an examiner conclude that there are signs of interference in Y1 to Y15?
Nurul: It depends on the type of interference found.
The inquest will resume in October. — Daily Express
3483d86824b21486: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today called for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be held as soon as possible, saying the time had come for Barisan Nasional (BN) to seek a fresh mandate to lead the country.
Zahid said GE16 would be a defining moment for Umno and BN to regain the mandate to lead, as he outlined the coalition’s “gelombang biru” (blue wave) strategy ahead of the next general election.

“Therefore, the time has come for GE16 to be held immediately. Do you agree?” he said in his fiery policy speech at Umno’s general assembly here, to which delegates in the Dewan Merdeka hall replied with a loud “Yes!”.
He then told delegates that since the party had already been fighting for its political position, it should see the battle through to the end.
“Since we have started, we might as well see it through to the end. Since we are already fighting, let us fight all the way,” he said.
Zahid said the political landscape had become more complex, with Malay politics no longer centred on a single political vehicle and voter loyalties no longer being inherited.
He said the younger generation was also less bound by nostalgia for the old political landscape, meaning Umno could no longer rely on a single formula in every electoral battleground.
“Demographics differ. Issues differ. Candidates differ. Sentiments also differ. That is the reality today,” he said.
Zahid said the results in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan had each offered different lessons for the party.
He said Sabah had provided a lesson, Johor had raised confidence, while Negri Sembilan showed that political understanding could be a strength.
“Melaka, God willing, will be the next battleground to test how far the ‘blue wave’ can truly be translated into action,” he said.
Zahid said the blue wave was not merely intended to make Umno a supporting component of the government.
“GE16 is the defining moment for us to regain the mandate to lead the country,” he said.
GE16 must be held by 2028 at the latest, unless Parliament is dissolved earlier.
f837b0d84cfcc400: DALLAS: Vice President JD Vance took center stage at the Republican convention in Dallas on Thursday in a speech seen as an early test of his 2028 White House prospects, offering a message of nationalistic pride that resonated with the pro-Trump crowd.

As party leaders grapple with slipping approval ratings and uncertainty over November's midterm elections, they are also looking for signs of who might eventually carry President Donald Trump's movement forward.

Trump followed Vance with closing remarks and offered little commentary from the stage on his vice president's high-profile appearance, instead imploring supporters to vote Republican on Nov 3, the stated purpose of the first-of-its-kind midterm convention.

But speaking to reporters later as he boarded Air Force One to return to Washington, Trump said Vance did "very well" and was a "very talented guy," adding: "He's been a great vice president, and I think he did a very good job."

The president has yet to signal who he would back in 2028, though Republicans frequently speculate about whether Vance or Secretary of State Marco Rubio is best positioned to lead the party after he leaves office.

With Trump constitutionally barred from seeking a third term, Vance is widely regarded as a leading contender for the nomination. He spoke of an "American birthright" to safety and prosperity that he said Democrats opposed.

“Don't give the country over to a bunch of crazy people because you happen to disagree with us on a policy issue here and there," Vance said, reinforcing a convention theme that cast Republicans as the party of common sense and Democrats as the party of "crazy."
Chants of '48, 48'
Vance's 40-minute speech stayed largely on script, unlike Trump's freewheeling speaking style, and at times resembled a presidential nominating convention speech.

But in one apparently spontaneous moment, a protester waved a Mexican flag, prompting Vance to respond, "Well, my friend, if you love Mexico so much, get your ass over there," triggering a loud round of applause and chants of "USA, USA, USA."
Vance then offered to buy the man a plane ticket.

Supporters cited the 42-year-old's youth and appeal to grassroots activists as reasons he is well positioned to advance the party's populist, anti-establishment agenda once Trump leaves the political stage.

Some in the crowd chanted "48, 48," suggesting Vance could become the country's 48th president in 2028, but Vance said Republicans first needed to concentrate on winning the November midterm elections.

Barbara Johnson, 58, joined the "JD" chants during Vance's speech. She said his love of America came through in his remarks and that she was impressed by the way he fed off the crowd, adding that he made a "pretty dang good argument" for becoming the Republican Party's next standard-bearer.
"He does have a gift and I think he is proving himself more and more that he could be the leader of the country," Johnson, who lives in Plano, Texas, told Reuters.

Before Vance took the stage, Republicans used the convention to portray Democrats as dangerous extremists ahead of November's midterm elections, with Senator Ted Cruz of Texas accusing them, without substantiation, of being part of a "new and dangerous red-green alliance" between communists and Islamists.
Future beyond Trump

Throughout the two-day gathering, speakers sought to energize Republican voters by focusing on immigration, crime and cultural issues – frequently attacking Muslim politicians – as the party confronts questions about its future beyond Trump.

Listing what he considered the ills of life under Democratic President Joe Biden from 2021 to 2025, Vance said, "We were tired of being called racist for noticing that our country was becoming dirtier and poorer and less safe and less prosperous."

There was less emphasis on issues that voters tell pollsters they are most concerned about such as the economy, especially inflation and the cost of living, and the US war on Iran, which has driven up fuel costs and has dragged on for much longer than the four or five weeks that Trump predicted early on.
Coast of Iran war

Vance has long been associated with the Republican Party's anti-interventionist wing and previously argued against a war with Iran. In recalling the memory of slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk on the first anniversary of his death, Vance noted, "Charlie hated war." But Vance did not distance himself from the US decision to go to war six months ago nor speak explicitly about his views on it.
Even if Thursday's program was supposed to showcase Vance, the visual cues inside the 20,000-seat arena pointed overwhelmingly to Trump.

Oversized photos of Trump lined the walls, including the image of him raising his fist after an assassination attempt in Butler, Pennsylvania, and a towering floor-to-ceiling poster showing him standing before massive steel coils at a factory.
When Trump followed Vance to the stage, he first promised to be brief after having spoken for two hours the night before and saying, "I don't feel like going over the same material again."

But in his 25-minute speech he soon reverted to the speaking style he has employed at political rallies over the years, reciting a list of perceived grievances against the news media and his political opponents, unverified stories and exaggerations interspersed with occasional verifiable statements.
At one point he implored the crowd to repeat his words, which included referring to himself as "the greatest president in the history of the US."
Trump made a final plea for election turnout, telling supporters they would "go to hell" if they did not vote in November.
61a1ec6c5b9f1b2d: PARIS: Rhinestone-studded microphones in hand and decked out in glittery gowns, thousands of fans packed into a sweltering Paris theatre to belt out Celine Dion's classics ahead of the superstar's long-awaited return.

Paris has come down with a serious case of Celine Dion fever ahead of the 58-year-old's first full concert on Saturday since revealing she was suffering from a rare neurological disorder that forced her off stage.

Those who missed out on tickets for the French-Canadian chanteuse's 26 upcoming shows are finding other ways to join the frenzy - including giant karaoke parties where fans can sing their hearts out, even if they won't get to see their idol in person.
Some were more on-pitch than others.
"We're all singing terribly out of tune, and we're proud of it," said Sebastien Bonnet, 41, sporting bedazzled star-shaped sunglasses and sparkles dotted across his cheeks.
Bonnet was among some 2,600 fans who piled into the Grand Rex, a landmark theatre in central Paris, for a sold-out mass singalong organised by L'Ecran Pop.
Inside the Art Deco venue, fans snapped up Celine Dion-themed swag, from pink hats emblazoned with "My Heart Will Go On" to golden microphones that quickly ran out.
However, the main attraction was the chance to sing their favourite hits at the top of their lungs.
'Getting me ready'
Even before the live karaoke show began, her songs drifted through all three floors of the venue, drawing fans into impromptu singalongs.
Those who were slightly more in tune got the chance to join the band on stage after auditioning earlier in the evening.
Chiara, a 31-year-old singing teacher, and Antoine, a 23-year-old professional singer, took on the beloved French-language classic "J'irai où tu iras" (I'll Go Where You Go) before a fired-up crowd.
"The atmosphere tonight is amazing - it's getting me ready for the concert," said Chiara, still buzzing after stepping off stage.
While fans enthusiastically tackled songs from across Dion's catalogue, her French-language hits proved particular crowd-pleasers.
Her English songs "aren't really my thing," said Patricia, a retiree from Paris's western suburbs - a sentiment shared by her friend Rose and several other attendees.
For many in the crowd, the night was about more than just singing along.
One of the event's co-organisers, Clement Henaut, has been a fan for as long as he can remember, growing up with Dion's music as a constant soundtrack to car rides with his mother.
He has since crossed paths with the singer twice.
"I even gave her a kiss on the cheek," he said.
'Sad for a month'
However, when tickets for Dion's comeback went on sale through a lottery system, Henaut and some of the team behind L'Ecran Pop came up empty-handed.
"Like everyone else, I tried to get tickets during those dreadful days," he said.
The disappointment helped spark the idea for a karaoke night aimed at fellow fans who had also missed out on the real thing.
Corinne Abitbol, a pensioner in a gold sequin dress who came to sing with friends from choir, knew the feeling.
"I think I was sad for at least a month," she said, although the evening's festivities "make up for it a bit".
For one of Abitbol's fellow choir members, Angelique Reuard, the night offered a chance to revisit the music and memories of her adolescence.
"It's about reconnecting with that time in my teenage years," she said.
Beneath the sequins, singalongs and nostalgia was also relief at seeing a star return to the stage after years in which many fans feared she might never perform again.
"We missed her," said Carole, a 51-year-old primary teacher who attended the soiree with a group of colleagues.
"Celine is a phoenix," she said.
dcbba29b3cc64ae4: PETALING JAYA: Mahkamah Tinggi Alor Setar menolak permohonan GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutifnya, Nasiruddin Ali, untuk mencabar fatwa negeri dikenakan ke atas mereka tahun lalu.

Fatwa itu yang dikeluarkan Jawatankuasa Fatwa Negeri Kedah pada 20 Feb 2025, mengisytiharkan GISBH sebagai pertubuhan mempromosikan ajaran sesat, serta menambah sesiapa mengamalkannya dianggap melanggar enakmen syariah negeri.
Cabaran undang-undang dikemuka GISBH dan Nasiruddin gagal selepas Hakim Evawani Farisyta Mohammad memutuskan mahkamah sivil tidak mempunyai bidang kuasa mendengar kes tersebut.

"Permohonan semakan kehakiman ini bertujuan untuk mempersoal kandungan fatwa dan memohon mahkamah membatalkannya, bertentangan dengan dakwaan peguam bahawa mereka hanya menyemak proses pembuatan keputusan," katanya.
Evawani berkata, mahkamah sivil dilarang mendengar perkara yang berada di bawah bidang kuasa Mahkamah Syariah.
Mahkamah juga menyatakan, bahawa fatwa negeri berkenaan melibatkan kuasa prerogatif Sultan.
"Perkenan Kebawah Duli Yang Maha Mulia Baginda Sultan diperlukan sebelum sesuatu fatwa boleh diputuskan oleh jawatankuasa fatwa negeri," katanya.
Awal tahun ini, Mahkamah Tinggi di Shah Alam dan Kangar turut menolak cabaran oleh GISBH dan Nasiruddin terhadap fatwa sama yang dikeluarkan di negeri terbabit atas alasan sama.
GISBH dan Nasiruddin memfailkan rayuan terhadap tiga keputusan tersebut.
3beb37f9f58a02bf: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno menggesa agar cukai barangan dan perkhidmatan (GST) diperkenalkan semula pada kadar lebih munasabah dan menolak cadangan sistem hibrid yang menggabungkan GST dengan cukai jualan dan perkhidmatan (SST).
Presiden Umno, Zahid Hamidi, berkata ia perlu dilaksanakan semula dengan pendekatan mengambil kira kepentingan rakyat, perniagaan dan pembangunan ekonomi negara.
“Ubah semula sistem percukaian kepada GST. Tiada hibrid. Tiada negara yang menggunakan sistem hibrid.
“Insya-Allah, tekad kami adalah untuk mengembalikan GST dalam sistem percukaian negara pada kadar yang lebih munasabah,” katanya dalam ucapan dasar pada Perhimpunan Agung Umno di sini hari ini.
Menurut Zahid, pelaksanaan semula GST perlu mengambil kira kepentingan rakyat dan pada masa sama diselaraskan dengan jaminan sosial.
Katanya, sistem percukaian negara bukan sekadar bertujuan meningkatkan hasil kerajaan, sebaliknya perlu membantu memudahkan urusan perniagaan serta menyokong pembangunan ekonomi.
“Kita berazam untuk menyelaraskan jaminan sosial rakyat, memudahkan urusan perniagaan serta membangunkan ekonomi wilayah berasaskan kekuatan Semenanjung, belakang kita di Sarawak dan Sabah,” katanya.
Tambahnya, pendekatan percukaian itu selari dengan gagasan 'Malaysia Biru' yang dibawa Umno untuk membina negara yang lebih sejahtera dan berdaya tahan.
Menerusi gagasan itu katanya, ukuran kemajuan negara tidak seharusnya hanya berdasarkan pertumbuhan Keluaran Dalam Negara Kasar (KDNK), sebaliknya mengambil kira pendapatan boleh guna rakyat.

“Kita berhasrat untuk menjadikan Malaysia sebagai sebuah negara sejahtera. Kita mesti berani mengubah dan cara kita menilai kejayaan ekonomi. KDNK memang penting tetapi rakyat tidak hidup di dalam angka KDNK,” katanya.

Beliau berkata Umno mahu setiap keluarga mempunyai sekurang-kurangnya 30% pendapatan lebihan selepas keperluan asas dipenuhi, yang boleh digunakan untuk simpanan, pelaburan dan meningkatkan kualiti hidup.
"Sistem percukaian perlu menjadi sebahagian daripada usaha membina Malaysia sebagai negara yang mempunyai pemilikan aset, kemahiran dan daya tahan ekonomi.
0652a4a0da303718: TAIPEI: Micron Technology said on Friday its direct labour employees in Taiwan would receive bonuses equaling 35 to 68 months of pay for fiscal 2026, with minimum cash compensation of T$1.7 million (US$53,809.39), after the US chipmaker enjoyed what it described as an extraordinary year.
Micron said the payouts to the employees, including operators, technicians and shift engineers, were its strongest ever and that more than 60,000 employees globally will receive fiscal 2026 rewards.

The announcement comes after unions representing around two-thirds of Micron's workforce in Taiwan signalled widespread support among members for a strike. The unions did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The rewards include a T$1 million (US$31,652.58) cash bonus for Taiwan employees, who joined before August 29, 2025, for fiscal 2026, the US memory maker said.
For entry-level engineers, total rewards average T$3.4 million, including an average of T$2.9 million in cash compensation, with the remainder comprising equity at grant value, the company said.
Every employee will also receive an annual equity grant, Micron said.
Micron employs about 15,000 people in Taiwan, one of its most important manufacturing hubs, and said it has invested more than T$1.6 trillion in the island.
The US memory maker and the Taoyuan union failed to reach an agreement during a mediation meeting last week, with a second round of mediation scheduled.

Micron is looking to avoid being dragged into a crisis similar to what its Korean rival Samsung Electronics faced in May, when a planned 18-day strike by as many as 48,000 union members was called off after last-minute negotiations and a successful deal that created a special bonus pool worth 10.5% of the chip division's operating profit, subject to profitability targets.
Back then the prospect of a stoppage at the world's largest memory-chip maker had raised worries about chip supplies and broader economic fallout in Asia's fourth-largest economy.
Micron's Taiwanese unions previously said profit-sharing arrangements at Samsung and SK Hynix had widened the gap between Micron workers and their South Korean peers.
c3ed40870832950c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Asean and China are seeking to deepen their decade-long health cooperation as the region confronts emerging public health threats, climate change, demographic shifts and rapid technological transformation.

Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the partnership is entering an increasingly consequential chapter, with both sides working towards resilient, inclusive and sustainable health systems capable of responding to present and future challenges.

“Our gathering today comes at a defining moment as we face the rapidly evolving health landscape, shaped by emerging public health threats, climate change, demographic shifts and accelerating technological transformation.
“These challenges remind us that resilient health systems are no longer simply a national priority. They are a shared regional imperative,” he said.
He said this in his opening remarks when chairing the 10th Asean-China Health Ministers’ Meeting in conjunction with the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings here today.
The meeting was co-chaired with Vice-Minister of China’s National Health Commission Dr Liu Jinfeng.

Dzulkefly said discussions at the meeting, themed ‘Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future Ready Health Systems’, would also contribute to the implementation of the Asean Strategic Health Agenda (ASHA) 2026-2030 and translate common aspirations into practical action.
“The decisions and perspectives we share today have the potential to strengthen the health and resilience of more than two billion people across Asean and China.
“Let us seize this opportunity to build a decade of partnership and look ahead with renewed resolve to deepen our cooperation for the decades to come,” he added.

He said the meeting also aims to provide strategic direction in advancing the Asean-China Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on health cooperation, capture collective commitments through a Joint Statement and ensure the partnership delivers tangible benefits to the people. — Bernama
65d2657909e72e18: The president demonised Democrats in an attempt to wangle votes in midterms despite backlash over Iran war With his approval rating at a historic low, Donald Trump has brought down the curtain on the Republicans’ first ever midterm convention by pleading with supporters to do him “the biggest favour” and “pretend” they are voting for him in November’s US elections. The president is facing a growing backlash over rising prices and the war in Iran. Sweeping losses for the Republican party could effectively turn Trump into a lame duck for his final two years in the White House. Continue reading...
e3a3a0d8c35944fa: KUALA LUMPUR: Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi menyindir Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim, dengan berkata bahawa partinya boleh melakukan lebih baik dan menggesa beliau mendengar suara rakyat.
Zahid, yang juga timbalan perdana menteri, berkata demikian dalam ucapan dasar presiden pada Perhimpunan Agung Umno.

Ketika menggariskan agenda ekonomi, Zahid mengkritik perkara yang disifatkannya sebagai ketidakpastian berhubung dasar kerajaan, khususnya percukaian oleh Anwar yang dirujuk beliau sebagai 'guru' dalam ucapan itu.
“Cukup-cukuplah, guru! Dengarlah suara kami, guru! Dengarlah suara rakyat, wahai guru! Cukup-cukuplah!
“Insya-Allah, kami boleh buat lebih baik daripada yang guru buat,” katanya.
Zahid menegaskan teguran itu bukan bertujuan membakar api sebaliknya mahu memastikan keresahan rakyat tidak terus disemarakkan.
"Kita tidak mahu menimbulkan keresahan Kita tidak mahu menimbulkan kegelisahan apatah lagi menimbulkan kekeliruan yang menjadi kekeliruan yang tidak berkesudahan,” katanya.

Zahid juga berkata Umno mensasarkan 80% tenaga kerja negara ini berada dalam kategori berkemahiran tinggi dan memperoleh gaji lumayan serta mempunyai pemilikan terhadap rumah, saham dan harta intelek.

"Selama ini kita banyak mengukur kemajuan rakyat melalui pendapatan. Hakikatnya rakyat yang benar-benar berdaya maju mesti memempunyai rumah, perusahaan, saham, harta terutamanya harta intelek, simpanan mahupun aset produktif.

"Justeru, kita semua mahu negara ini bergerak daripada masyarakat yang hanya berpendapatan kepada masyarakat yang memiliki. Sasaran kita 60% daripada rakyat dewasa Malaysia memiliki secara langsung sekurang-kurangnya satu aset yang menjana nilai," katanya.
91a425077504884f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today took a veiled jibe at Pakatan Harapan’s past election manifesto to slash petrol prices within 24 hours if the coalition won the general election.

Speaking at the 2026 Umno General Assembly today, Ahmad Zahid said Umno is a far-sighted party with a long-term vision for Malaysia rather than one that merely hopes to survive one election after another.
“We are starting again after a fall,” he said, referring to Umno’s disastrous outing in GE14, held in 2018.
“From once ruling the country and being a dominant force, we have experienced being the opposition and then sharing power.
“Now, we are ready to create another victory,” he added.
Stressing that Umno would not make unrealistic promises, Zahid said: “We are also not a party that says, menang hari ini (win today)…” as the crowd responded, “minyak turun (fuel prices down)”.
Similarly, he also took a swipe at the PH-led unity government’s flip-flopping approach in withdrawing and later reinstating the subsidised fuel quota to 300 litres under the Budi95 programme.
“First, they reduce the quota, then they reinstate it. Next, I think they will pull it back and restore it nearer to the next general election.
“Who is doing this? Guru,” he said, drawing thunderous applause from the audience.
Zahid did not elaborate on whom he meant by “guru”, though the remark was widely seen as a veiled reference to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“God willing, we will be able to perform better than Guru has done,” he added.
d41be67468bb7c4f: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Budget 2027 should move Malaysia’s artificial intelligence (AI) agenda beyond data centre construction towards enterprise adoption, domestic intellectual property, cybersecurity and workforce productivity.

MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB) said there should also be focus on supply-side efficiency by broadening the tax base, closing leakages, expanding consumption excises, introducing carbon pricing, rationalising spending and crowding in private investment.

“Budget 2027 should not only be assessed through fiscal expenditure. It should also strengthen Malaysia’s broader investment ecosystem and the mobilisation of domestic capital,” it said in its Budget 2027 preview today.
MBSB IB emphasised that its wish list centres on policy certainty, transparent project implementation, outcome-based incentives and measures that channel long-term savings into productive investment.

“A successful budget would not merely provide near-term economic support, but it would improve access to growth capital, strengthen domestic capabilities and help translate Malaysia’s investment cycle into sustainable productivity, higher-quality employment and long-term economic value,” it added.
MBSB IB also emphasised that a multi-year project pipeline, with project values, tender timing, funding sources and execution milestones disclosed, should be published.
“This would improve planning and reduce speculative market movements,” it said.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9, 2026, and would be the fifth Madani Budget and the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan.

On the overall Budget 2027 allocation, MBSB IB said the budget is expected to remain moderately expansionary, with total federal government expenditure potentially reaching a new record of around RM440.9 billion, compared with Budget 2026’s RM421.2 billion.
“The larger allocation is likely to reflect higher operating expenditure, continued social and cost-of-living support, as well as higher development spending.
“Nevertheless, the increase is expected to remain measured as the government continues to balance the need to support economic growth with its medium-term fiscal consolidation objectives,” it said.
Development spending is expected to increase to between RM85 billion and RM90 billion, up from RM81 billion in Budget 2026.
On the fiscal deficit, MBSB IB said the deficit is expected to narrow to around 3.3 per cent to 3.5 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 2027.

Meanwhile, the investment bank said federal government revenue is expected to improve further in 2027, supported by increased direct and indirect tax collections on the back of sustained economic growth, continued efforts to broaden the revenue base and improved fiscal collections.

“For 2026, MOF had originally projected revenue of RM343.1 billion, underpinned by better tax collection and digitalisation initiatives. Total revenue is estimated to reach RM365.1 billion next year,” it added. — Bernama
46883169bcf0516d: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno wants the goods and services tax (GST) reintroduced at a more reasonable rate as part of its proposed “Malaysia Blue Agenda”, aimed at reshaping the country’s economic priorities.
Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the party rejected the proposed hybrid system combining GST with the current sales and service tax (SST).
“Change the taxation system back to GST. There is no hybrid. No country has a hybrid.
“God willing, our resolve is to bring GST back into the country’s taxation system at a more reasonable rate,” he said in his opening speech at the party’s general assembly here today.

The GST, a multi-stage consumption tax, was introduced in April 2015 by the Barisan Nasional administration at a rate of 6%, before being zero-rated in June 2018 and replaced by the SST in September 2018.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim recently said the government was open to studying a system that would integrate elements of the GST and SST to create a more progressive tax structure.
Zahid said introducing an adjusted GST on its own would strengthen social security, ease business operations, and help develop the regional economy.
He said the proposal was part of the eight-point “Malaysia Blue Agenda”, which BN and its partners would pursue if given the opportunity to lead the country again.

The agenda, which he said was aimed at preparing Malaysia for its centenary of independence, would focus on creating wealth, rebuilding human capital, expanding ownership, safeguarding welfare, preparing for crises, caring for the people, rebuilding trust, and protecting national interests.

He said the agenda’s ultimate aim was for Malaysia to become the world’s “most influential middle power” and would form part of Umno and BN’s efforts to reorganise the country’s priorities after they return to federal power.
9deccccf5c4bbb1b: PETALING JAYA: The High Court in Alor Setar today dismissed applications by GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and its CEO, Nasiruddin Ali, to initiate a legal challenge to a state fatwa imposed on them last year.

The fatwa, issued by the Kedah state fatwa committee on Feb 20 last year, declared GISBH an organisation promoting deviant teachings, and added that anyone who adheres to them would be in breach of the state’s shariah enactment.
GISBH and Nasiruddin’s legal challenge failed after Justice Evawani Farisyta Mohammad held that the civil courts had no jurisdiction to hear the matter.

"The judicial review applications aimed to question the fatwa's contents and to get the court to set aside them, contrary to counsel’s claim that they were merely reviewing the decision-making process," she said.
Evawani said the civil courts were barred from hearing matters under the shariah courts' jurisdiction.
The court also said the state fatwa involved the prerogative powers of the state's ruler.
"His Royal Highness's consent is needed before a fatwa can be decided by the state fatwa committee," she said.
Earlier this year, the High Courts in Shah Alam and Kangar also dismissed challenges by GISBH and Nasiruddin to similar fatwas issued in the states on the same grounds.
GISBH and Nasiruddin have filed appeals against all three decisions.
4a1a055b6bfd9b41: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi took a swipe at Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim today, saying his party could do better than the leader he referred to as “guru” (teacher), and urging him to listen to the people.
Zahid, who is also the Barisan Nasional chairman and deputy prime minister, said this in his opening speech at the Umno general assembly here .
Outlining BN’s proposed economic agenda, he criticised what he described as uncertainty surrounding government policies, particularly on taxation.
“Who did this? Guru. Enough, guru. Listen to our voices, guru. We can do better than what the guru has done,” he said.
He said his criticism was not intended to incite hostility or undermine anyone.
“I am not trying to incite or provoke anyone. But we do not want to create anxiety or unease, let alone endless confusion,” he said.
Zahid also said enforcement agencies must not be used as political tools, amid recent speculation that senior Umno leaders may be arrested after the general assembly concludes.

“We do not want anyone to be put in orange or purple uniforms. We want them to be treated fairly,” he said, referring to the clothes worn by those detained by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission or the police.
Zahid also reiterated his call for the 16th general election to be held sooner, saying Umno and BN were ready to seek a fresh mandate.
He said Umno would seek to work with other political parties through a “grand collaboration”, based on political understanding rather than formal mergers.
This was necessary to avoid electoral clashes that would benefit neither side, and such collaboration would not require Umno or BN to abandon their identities.
Zahid said Umno’s ultimate goal was to return BN to federal power and implement what he described as the “Malaysia Blue Agenda” ahead of the country’s centenary of independence.

He said the agenda would focus on creating wealth, rebuilding human capital, expanding ownership, safeguarding welfare, preparing for crises, caring for the people, rebuilding trust, and protecting national interests.
94749f8a659a2ea9: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Providing homeownership assistance, particularly for youths and gig workers, is among the key priorities of the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035, ensuring greater access to affordable housing.

Ministry of Housing and Local Government (known by its Malay initials KPKT) Deputy Secretary-General (Housing and Urban Wellbeing) Zulkeflee Sulaiman said the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) was among the mechanisms available to help first-time homebuyers without a fixed income or payslips.
“SJKP can help first-time homebuyers, particularly gig workers who do not have payslips, to secure housing loans, with the Government acting as a guarantor through participating banks.
“The Government wants to make sure young people who want to own their first home are not left behind,” he said when appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme here yesterday.

Launched by Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming on Aug 10, the DRN 2026-2035 sets the direction for the national housing sector over the next decade, covering six focus areas, 17 strategies and 59 action plans.

Zulkeflee said the policy also includes measures to address strata management issues, with amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013 expected to be brought to the Government next year before being tabled in Parliament.

Meanwhile, KPKT Housing Planning Division undersecretary J. Murali said the ministry was refining the national affordable housing guidelines, with location being among the factors considered in determining prices.
He said setting RM300,000 as a nationwide benchmark might not be suitable, as affordability and market conditions varied between Kuala Lumpur and states such as Perlis, Sabah and Sarawak.
“We already have the framework and are now refining it. We will come up with national affordable housing guidelines which will be launched later,” he said.
Murali said that, apart from pricing, the ministry was also taking into account tenant welfare, despite the country’s 76 per cent homeownership rate.
As such, he said a Residential Tenancy Act would be introduced to provide clearer protection for tenants while also safeguarding property owners’ interests.

Murali said the DRN 2026-2035 would involve the drafting of three new pieces of legislation, namely the Property Development Act, Building Managers Act and Residential Tenancy Act, as well as amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013. — Bernama
7b1245c4ac9eb8d4: KUALA LUMPUR: Seorang senator Sarawak menolak perbandingan antara pertikaian Petronas-Petros dengan kontroversi Tabung Haji (TH), dengan mengatakan bahawa kedua-dua perkara itu pada asasnya berbeza.

Robert Lau berkata pertikaian yang melibatkan Petronas dan Petros milik kerajaan Sarawak itu berkaitan dengan hak perlembagaan, kuasa perundangan dan pelaksanaan kuasa persekutuan secara sejarah, bukannya dakwaan rasuah, penyelewengan atau salah urus dana awam.

Beliau menjawab ulasan pakar tadbir urus, Walter Sandosam yang disiarkan Malay Mail semalam, yang mengingatkan bahawa penyelesaian antara Petronas dan Petros boleh berdepan kritikan jika ia dilihat sebagai kompromi politik dan bukannya keputusan yang dibuat demi kepentingan negara.

Sandosam, bekas presiden Institut Juruaudit Dalaman Malaysia dan bekas anggota panel perundingan dan pencegahan rasuah Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia, membuat perbandingan dengan TH dan Felda, di mana keputusan terdahulu dikaji semula berikutan kebimbangan mengenai tadbir urus dan pengawasan.
Lau berkata perbandingan itu tidak mengambil kira perbezaan asas sifat pertikaian Petronas-Petros.
“TH pada asasnya merupakan perkara berkaitan tadbir urus institusi dan pengurusan kewangan,” katanya.

Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja baru-baru ini telah membangkitkan persoalan serius berhubung pengurusan dan pelaburan TH, termasuk pelaksanaan kuasa oleh mereka yang dipertanggungjawabkan untuk menguruskan institusi itu.
“Begitu juga dengan Felda dan beberapa agensi persekutuan lain yang diuruskan secara salah.”

Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja baru-baru ini membangkitkan persoalan serius berhubung pengurusan dan pelaburan TH, termasuk pelaksanaan kuasa oleh mereka yang dipertanggungjawabkan untuk menguruskan institusi itu.
“Begitu juga dengan Felda dan beberapa agensi persekutuan lain yang diuruskan secara salah.”
Beliau berkata kebimbangan berhubung TH dan Felda melibatkan tadbir urus serta kesannya terhadap ekonomi negara, tetapi tidak menyentuh kedudukan perlembagaan negara.
“Pertikaian Petros-Petronas mempunyai sifat yang sama sekali berbeza,” tambahnya.
“Ia berkaitan dengan hubungan perlembagaan dan undang-undang antara Sarawak dengan Persekutuan.

"Ia melibatkan Perjanjian Malaysia 1963 (MA63), Perlembagaan Persekutuan, kedudukan dan sempadan perlembagaan negeri-negeri, serta kuasa masing-masing kerajaan persekutuan dan kerajaan negeri berhubung sumber petroleum.”
Lau berkata dimensi politik tidak secara automatik menjadikan sesuatu pertikaian itu sebagai kegagalan akauntabiliti.

“Dalam sesebuah persekutuan, pertikaian perlembagaan boleh dan sering memerlukan penentuan kehakiman serta rundingan politik,” katanya, sambil memetik Kanada dan Australia sebagai contoh sistem persekutuan yang menggunakan penyelesaian politik bagi menyelesaikan pertikaian sedemikian.

“Mahkamah mempunyai peranan dalam menentukan persoalan undang-undang. Pemimpin politik mempunyai peranan dalam menyelesaikan perkara yang menyentuh hubungan antara bahagian-bahagian yang membentuk persekutuan.”
Beliau berkata penyelesaian politik yang selaras dengan Perlembagaan Persekutuan dan MA63 tidak seharusnya diketepikan sebagai kompromi politik yang tidak boleh diterima.
5c40e50e9c4d59a6: NEW YORK: Elena Rybakina rallied from a set down to beat Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 on Thursday and book a US Open championship showdown with two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka.
In Saturday's final Rybakina will try to deal another blow to Sabalenka, having knocked her out of the number one world ranking just by reaching the semi-finals.
"I feel like I definitely need to step my game up, serve much better than today and stay aggressive," Rybakina said of her looming clash with Sabalenka.

Gauff's bid to return to the final for the first time since she defeated Sabalenka for the 2023 title had got off to a smooth start, with the American seizing the initiative in the opening set with a break to go 4-2 up.
She held to love to take a 5-2 lead and then held in the ninth game to take a one set lead.
But Rybakina hit back with an early break of serve in the second set for a 3-1 lead and held to go 4-1 up.
Gauff responded superbly to claw her way back into contention with a break to make it 4-3 before holding to square it a 4-4.
Yet she was unable to make the most of her fightback and double-faulted in the 10th game to hand two set points to Rybakina at 15-40. Rybakina pounced on that chance to take the match to a third set.
The decisive set followed a similar pattern.
Gauff conceded a break to trail 5-3 and leave Rybakina serving for the match.
But the American broke back immediately to make it 5-4 to get it back on serve.
Again though Gauff was unable to capitalise, and a deft volley from Rybakina left her with two match points at 15-40, before Gauff then hit a wide open smash long to hand her opponent victory.

c513a29756fdf53e: SINGAPORE, Sept 11 — Singapore’s air quality has improved, with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) in all five regions remaining in the moderate range since 10pm yesterday, The Straits Times reported.

The other four regions also recorded readings within the moderate range as at 7am.
According to the report, the haze in Singapore had worsened from Sept 4, when the PSI in the central region crossed the 101 mark, considered unhealthy.
Since then, the central, eastern and western regions have occasionally recorded unhealthy readings before returning to the moderate range, the report said.
In an advisory yesterday, NEA forecast the 24-hour PSI to range from the higher end of the moderate category to the lower end of the unhealthy range.
NEA said it continued to observe moderate to dense smoke plumes from fires in southern and central Sumatra as well as Kalimantan, with some haze drifting towards Singapore.

It added that while some showers were forecast mainly over northern and central Sumatra in the coming days, there remained a risk of smoke haze affecting Singapore if the fires persisted under prevailing south-easterly or southerly winds, The Straits Times reported.
The recent deterioration marked the first time Singapore’s PSI reached unhealthy levels due to haze since October 2023.
A PSI reading of 51 to 100 is considered moderate, while readings between 101 and 200 are classified as unhealthy, during which NEA advises the public to reduce outdoor activities.

d036a4d4d5499ca1: KUALA LUMPUR: A Sarawak senator has rejected a comparison between the Petronas-Petros dispute and the Tabung Haji (TH) controversy, saying the two matters are fundamentally different.

Robert Lau said the row involving Petronas and Sarawak’s state-owned Petros concerned constitutional rights, legislative authority and the historical exercise of federal power, not allegations of corruption, embezzlement or mismanagement of public funds.

He was responding to a commentary by governance specialist Walter Sandosam, carried by Malay Mail yesterday, which cautioned that a settlement between Petronas and Petros could face scrutiny if it is seen as a political compromise rather than a decision made in national interests.

Sandosam, a former president of the Institute of Internal Auditors Malaysia and former member of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's consultation and corruption prevention panel, drew comparisons with TH and Felda, where past decisions were revisited over concerns about governance and oversight.
Lau said the comparison overlooked the fundamentally different nature of the Petronas-Petros dispute.
"TH is fundamentally an institutional governance and financial management matter," he said.
"The recent royal commission of inquiry has raised serious questions concerning the management and investment of TH, including the exercise of powers by those entrusted with managing the institution.
"Likewise for Felda and several other federal agencies that are mismanaged."
He said the concerns surrounding TH and Felda involved governance and their impact on the national economy, but did not concern the constitutional position of the country.
"The Petros-Petronas dispute is of an entirely different character," he added.

"It concerns the constitutional and legal relationship between Sarawak and the federation. It engages the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), the Federal Constitution, the constitutional position and boundaries of the states, and the respective powers of the federal and state governments concerning petroleum resources."
Lau said a political dimension did not automatically turn a dispute into an accountability failure.

"In a federation, constitutional disputes can and often do require both judicial determination and political negotiation," he said, citing Canada and Australia as examples of federal systems where political settlements are used to resolve such disputes.
"The courts have their role in determining questions of law. Political leaders have their role in resolving matters that concern the relationship between the constituent parts of the federation."
He said a political settlement consistent with the Federal Constitution and MA63 should not be dismissed as an unacceptable political compromise.
"Political compromise is not synonymous with corruption, nor does negotiation necessarily mean surrendering accountability," he said.

Lau also said Section 3 of the Petroleum Development Act 1974 provided for a political solution, as it empowers the prime minister to issue directions to Petronas that are binding on the national oil company.
He said the historical context behind Sarawak’s present claim also required scrutiny.
Lau said the Continental Shelf Act 1966, which was enacted for the Federation of Malaya, was extended to Sarawak and Sabah in 1969 through executive powers under the Emergency Ordinance 1969.

He said Sarawak and Sabah had their own pre-Malaysia laws governing their continental shelves, and questioned the legal and constitutional basis for using emergency powers arising from circumstances in Malaya to alter their legal position.
"The people of Sarawak are not asking for a favour," he said.
"They are asking that the constitutional settlement upon which Malaysia was formed be examined and honoured."
Lau said any settlement reached after the courts determine the legal questions should not be regarded as a failure of accountability if it is constitutional and mutually acceptable.
"It may instead be the very exercise of constitutional responsibility that has been missing for decades," he said.

777a51e526c5bf7a: HONG KONG: A Hong Kong court handed three Tiananmen vigil activists jail sentences of between five and seven years on Friday for national security crimes, following a trial that has drawn international condemnation.

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, Chow Hang-tung, 41, and Albert Ho, 74, have been behind bars since being charged in 2021, and their convictions -- under a national security law Beijing imposed on Hong Kong -- have been condemned by the UN, rights groups, and foreign governments.
A court ruled in August that the activists had breached the Chinese constitution by calling for an "end to one-party dictatorship".
Lee and Chow, who pleaded not guilty, were sentenced to seven years and seven years and three months respectively, AFP journalists in court heard.
Ho, a former lawmaker who pleaded guilty in January, received five years and two months.
Chow, a barrister, represented herself, told a hearing last month that she rejected the convictions, adding that she had "nothing to repent for".
The three activists arrived at court smiling and waving to supporters before being escorted into the docks.

Hong Kong and Macau were formerly the only places on Chinese soil that permitted public vigils to mourn those killed on June 4, 1989, when Beijing sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform in and around the capital's Tiananmen Square.
But public commemoration has been effectively banned in Hong Kong since the Beijing-imposed security law took effect.
The trio were leaders of the now-defunct Hong Kong Alliance, the group that organised annual vigils in the city's Victoria Park.
'Erase memories'
The group also operated a museum dedicated to the crackdown and held events, including a yearly washing of the "Pillar of Shame" -- a statue to mourn victims.
The statue was dismantled and removed from its long-time plinth at the University of Hong Kong in late 2021, and other local universities followed suit with similar objects.
Prosecutors argued that evidence in the case, including the statue and archives from the Hong Kong Alliance's museum, should be confiscated.
Judge Alex Lee said on Friday the fate of the statue would be decided after a decision was made on its ownership.
Ahead of Friday's sentencing, Chow said "the authorities' true intentions were finally laid bare".
"This prosecution is an attempt to erase memories, particularly those of June 4, by reading too much into certain slogans," she said.
The Danish artist behind "Pillar of Shame", Jens Galschiot, called the outcome of the trial and the statue's potential confiscation "outrageous".
"This is an attack on my private ownership and my artist's work... if they confiscate it," he told AFP.
The statue tells the story of Tiananmen, said Galschiot, who has for years sought to reclaim his work.
If it were destroyed, that would also "destroy the story that everybody should know".

783ad2418c67fce9: MIRI, Sept 11 — “This story may soon be forgotten by others, bit by bit, but I will never forget you, not even for a second.”

Those were the anguished words posted on Threads by izzatisyamimi, wife of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, who was among five people killed when a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crashed near Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8.
Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.

Posting under the handle izzatisyamimi shortly after midnight on Sept 10, just hours after her husband’s DNA sample was sent for testing and a day after his body was recovered, the widow poured out her grief in a message that has since been widely shared on social media.

“People see me as strong on the outside, but inside I am completely shattered,” she wrote. “You always said I was a supermom, you always said I was a strong woman, but who am I without you by my side? You taught me to be strong, but it isn’t fair of you to leave me like this. I did tell you to fly high, but this time you flew too high — so high that I can no longer catch up with you. Love you always.”

A day earlier, as the bodies of the victims were being recovered from the crash site, the same account had posted another message addressed directly to her late husband, describing the couple’s children crying inconsolably through the night.

“Your children really aren’t giving me any chance to cry at all, are they? Please help settle them for a while, daddy — my pool of tears is already full. It’s my turn now. Tonight both of them were wailing. Just be patient, it’s my turn now. I hope you’re strong enough to watch me cry my heart out. We love you daddy,” she wrote.

The others who died in their FDS mission to serve the rural people of Sarawak were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.

The tragedy has also prompted an outpouring of recollections from villagers, former colleagues, friends and family members of the crew, many of whom took to social media to share memories of the FDS team’s outreach trips across Kapit, Limbang and Miri divisions.
Among the widely circulated tributes was a video and photo montage sourced from TikTok user Fikri Jalil, showing the FDS team during a visit to Kampung Balai in Ulu Baram.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Among the images were a doctor attending to a patient on the steps of a longhouse, villagers chatting warmly with the pilot during a stopover, and locals helping the crew load medical supplies and equipment back onto the aircraft.
The accompanying caption recalled the crew’s parting words to the villagers: “We’ll come again in November, okay?”

“These, it turned out, were the last words spoken before they left Kampung Balai, Ulu Baram,” the post read. “That promise, now impossible to keep, has become a heart-wrenching memory for villagers still grieving over this tragedy. Their service and sacrifice to the villagers will never be forgotten. Al-Fatihah.”
Among the five victims was paramedic the late Jessie Paya Jok, 44, who according to a close friend had been just months away from beginning a new chapter in her life.

Her friend of nearly two decades, Caroline Sawai Joseph Chungat, said Paya had excitedly shared that this month was to be her last serving with the FDS. She had planned to pursue an Advanced Diploma in Midwifery thereafter.
“Next year I want to continue my studies…” was how Paya had put it to those close to her, Chungat recalled — an ambition that never came to pass.

Chungat, who had known Paya since 2005, described her as a soft-spoken woman of few words who nonetheless brightened the lives of those around her with her smile. During her service at the Bario Health Clinic, Paya was remembered fondly by residents of the interior, including for reportedly using her own money at times to help cover the travel fares of patients who needed treatment at Miri Hospital.

“Not everyone’s good deeds are spoken of while they are still alive. Sometimes, it is only after they are gone that we truly realise the extent of the kindness they showed,” Chungat’s tribute read, adding that although Paya’s dream went unfulfilled, her service and kindness would continue to be remembered by those whose lives she touched.
“Al-Fatihah for the late Jessie Paya Jok. May all her sacrifices become deeds that continue to bring reward,” the tribute concluded.

The helicopter, which was ferrying an FDS medical team, went down near Long Lellang in Ulu Baram on Sept 8, killing all five people on board. Recovery operations for the victims’ remains were carried out over the following days, with DNA samples taken to confirm their identities.

The FDS provides outreach medical and health services to remote interior communities across Sarawak, with teams regularly flown by helicopter to longhouses and villages inaccessible by road. — The Borneo Post

8d60ccb8507dbd62: PARIS, Sept 11 — Fans of Canadian superstar Celine Dion are gearing up for an onstage comeback many feared might never happen, with just a day to go until her opening concert in Paris following a years-long battle with a rare neurological disorder.

The 58-year-old will on Saturday perform her first full concert since revealing she was suffering from Stiff Person Syndrome, an incurable condition that forced her to cancel shows and left her struggling to sing.
Some 30,000 fans of the “My Heart Will Go On” singer are expected to see her reclaim the spotlight each night of her 26-date run in the French capital.
“I’m really, really, really looking forward to it – and the closer it gets, the more excited I am,” said fan Elsa, who is going to one of the October shows with her sister and friends.
“We’re always singing her songs at karaoke, and so many of them bring back those memories,” said the 39-year-old, who preferred not to give her full last name.
She said she had been due to see Dion once before only for the concert to be cancelled after the singer fell ill – making her all the more determined not to miss out this time.
“She’s one of those artists – one of the very few – I really wanted to fight to get a ticket for,” she said.
‘Goosebumps’
Dion – whose hits include “It’s All Coming Back to Me Now” and “Because You Loved Me” – has sold around 260 million albums in English and French over a four-decade career.
She kicks off her residency at the Plenitude Arena outside Paris on Saturday evening, with 16 sold-out shows in September and October before returning for another 10 next May.
Resale tickets are scarce, with one site showing just two seats available for her September 26 show listed at an eye-watering €1,035 (RM4,882) and another at €862.
Hotel prices are also seeing a boost, with holiday booking site Kayak showing a 50 per cent bump on some of her concert dates.
Florence Monsellier, a 36-year-old French IT project manager, was “absolutely delighted” to have secured six seats.
“I’ll be going with my mum, my sister and my three cousins,” said the self-described “lifelong fan”, who last saw Dion perform in 2007.
Even those without tickets may still get a chance to see the global superstar.
Admirers have gathered outside the Royal Monceau hotel each day, where Dion has regularly emerged for impromptu exchanges with fans.

Videos posted on social media show Dion singing and dancing with fans, even seemingly taking the phone number of one after being impressed by his rendition of her new single “Bonjour, Pardon, Merci” (Hello, Excuse Me, Thank you).
Stephanie, who works near the Royal Monceau, told AFP she left work early one day last week to make sure she saw the singer after narrowly missing her the night before.
“She put on a show... I got goosebumps,” said Stephanie, who declined to give her last name.
Six-year wait
Dion’s return to the stage caps a comeback that, for years, was far from certain.
The singer revealed in December 2022 that she had been diagnosed with a rare and incurable autoimmune disorder that can cause severe muscle stiffness and agonising spasms.
The illness forced Dion to cancel concerts, but she repeatedly vowed to fight her way back to the stage.
“I’m going to come onstage because I’m ready. And my vocal cords will not scare me, because I’m going to be ready, and I’m going to hit those notes,” she told NBC two years ago.
She stunned fans with a surprise appearance at the 2024 Paris Olympics opening ceremony, belting out the Edith Piaf classic “Hymn to Love” from the Eiffel Tower.
For Elsa, watching Dion retake the stage, however briefly, was emotional.
“By the end of her song, I was crying like a baby,” she said.
Now, with her return to a full-length concert just days away, Dion has kept much of the show – including its setlist – under wraps, while teasing fans with a few hints and some practical advice.
“Usually I do a one-hour-40-minute show, but this one’s longer,” she told the crowd one night.
Her tip for those lucky enough to have tickets: “Make sure you wear good shoes.” — AFP

f3f0edd1d3c9432b: SEPTEMBER 11 — “It’s okay. Just this once.”
“I’ve worked hard.”
“I deserve this.”
Many of us have probably said something similar before buying something we did not really need.
Perhaps it was a new pair of shoes. A handbag. Another skincare product. An expensive cup of coffee. Or something that had been sitting in our online shopping cart for several days.
We know we could live without it.
But after a long week, a stressful day at work or simply a day that did not go particularly well, the purchase suddenly feels justified.
We call it a reward.
Sometimes, we call it self-care.
And this is where something interesting is happening in contemporary consumer culture.
Taking care of ourselves is becoming increasingly associated with buying something.

Self-care, of course, does not require a transaction. Getting enough sleep is self-care. Resting is self-care. Going for a walk, exercising, spending time with family or simply giving ourselves permission to do nothing for a while can all be forms of self-care.
Yet look at the language surrounding self-care in consumer culture today.
Treat yourself.
You deserve it.
Invest in yourself.
Because you’re worth it.
These phrases connect products with something much bigger than what those products actually do.
We are not simply buying skincare. We are “taking care of ourselves”.
We are not simply going on holiday. We are “healing”.
We are not simply buying coffee. We are giving ourselves a “little treat”.
And we are not simply buying something we want.
We are “rewarding ourselves”.
This is not entirely accidental.
The marketplace has become remarkably good at offering products for the emotions we are experiencing.
When we are tired, there is something we can buy to make ourselves feel better.
When we are stressed, there is something that promises a little pleasure.
When we achieve something, there is a product waiting to become our reward.
Buying, in other words, is becoming part of our emotional vocabulary.
Consumer research has long recognised that consumption is not simply a rational act of satisfying needs. People also consume for pleasure, experiences, symbols and meanings.
But the digital environment has made the distance between emotion and purchase remarkably short.
The scale of Malaysia’s e-commerce economy gives us some indication of just how embedded digital transactions have become.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The digital environment has made the distance between emotion and purchase remarkably short. — AFP pic
According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), income from e-commerce transactions reached RM1.288 trillion in 2024, up 8.8 per cent from RM1.184 trillion in the previous year.

Much of this, of course, is not individual consumer spending. Business-to-business (B2B) transactions remained the largest component at RM879.6 billion, while business-to-government (B2G) transactions accounted for RM33.8 billion.
But the figure particularly relevant to consumers is business-to-consumer (B2C) e-commerce.
B2C transactions reached RM374.7 billion in 2024, an increase of 11.3 per cent from RM336.6 billion a year earlier.
These figures tell us more than simply that Malaysians are buying online.
They point to a marketplace that is increasingly woven into the routines of everyday life — always available, easily accessible and often only a few taps away.
More importantly, we increasingly do not even have to go looking for something to buy.
The products come looking for us.

We open social media to watch videos, follow creators or simply pass the time. Somewhere between the entertainment, however, we encounter product demonstrations, reviews, shopping links and livestreams.

According to TikTok Shop, almost six in 10 of its users in Malaysia now choose LIVE shopping as their preferred shopping format. Sales generated through LIVE grew 48 per cent year-on-year and now account for almost a third of sales on the platform.
The significance of these figures goes beyond the popularity of livestream shopping.
They show how the boundary between entertainment and consumption is becoming increasingly difficult to see.
We may open TikTok because we want to unwind after a long day, not because we intend to shop.

Yet within the same space, we can discover a product, watch someone demonstrate it, hear why other people love it, encounter a limited-time offer and complete the purchase without ever leaving the platform.
From feeling tired, to becoming interested, to thinking “I deserve this”, and finally to checkout — the entire journey can happen within minutes.
The ability to buy also no longer depends entirely on how much money we have at that particular moment.
In 2025, Malaysians made 243 million Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) transactions worth RM21.3 billion.
That represented a sharp increase from 146 million transactions worth RM12 billion in 2024.
By the end of 2025, Malaysia had 7.5 million active BNPL users. Consumers aged 30 and below accounted for about 40 per cent of BNPL transactions.
But another number is particularly interesting.
The average BNPL transaction was only around RM91.
BNPL was also commonly used for food, groceries, transport and services.
This matters because consumer culture does not always manifest itself through extravagant handbags, expensive holidays or luxury purchases.
Increasingly, it can come through amounts that feel small enough to justify.
RM12 for coffee does not sound like much.
RM29 for a personal-care product hardly feels excessive.
RM45 for something on sale can even feel like a bargain.
And when payment itself can be divided into several instalments, the question “Can I afford this?” can gradually become “How much do I need to pay today?”
But perhaps what is even more interesting is how we explain these purchases to ourselves.
We rarely say, “I bought this because I was stressed.”
Instead, we say, “I wanted to reward myself.”
We do not say, “I was persuaded to buy this.”
We say, “What’s wrong with treating myself once in a while?” And perhaps the most powerful phrase of all is:
“I deserve this.”
Those three words turn a purchase into something more than a want.
They give consumption a form of justification.
I worked hard, therefore I deserve it.
I have sacrificed a lot, therefore I am entitled to enjoy something.
I am going through a difficult time, therefore I should do something that makes me happy.
There is nothing inherently wrong with any of this.
We should not feel guilty every time we buy coffee after a difficult day, purchase a pair of shoes we have wanted for months or take a holiday after working hard.
Consumption can bring pleasure.
And pleasure has a legitimate place in our lives.
Perhaps, then, the question is not whether we should stop buying things.
The question is when buying becomes our automatic response to how we feel.
This is where the culture of the “little treat” becomes interesting.

782ca8a12149b1bd: To federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh. From Boo Jia Cher
Dear Minister,

Throughout your career in public service, you have consistently represented a refreshing brand of political energy. Whether championing youth engagement, advocating for vulnerable communities, or defending green spaces in Kuala Lumpur, you bring a pragmatic determination to make our institutions work for ordinary people.

It is precisely this drive for tangible reform that leads me to write to you about the long-neglected, unsafe core of our capital city: the historic precinct around Masjid Jamek, Medan Pasar and Jalan Tun Perak.
A first-hand encounter

One evening, I stepped off the train at the Masjid Jamek LRT station. The transition from the bustling station to the sidewalk below was immediate and eerie. Walking down a quiet street, I saw a man lingering in the shadows with an unsettling smile, suggestive of ill intentions. Nervous, I quickened my pace, noticing only a few individuals seeking shelter in five-footways or battling addiction on the fringes. The streets were otherwise devoid of everyday life.

Billions of ringgit have been poured into the River of Life project and cosmetic heritage schemes, yet the historic birthplace of Kuala Lumpur remains an urban void the moment office workers head home.
The real problem

The core issue is not cosmetic investment, but a failure of urban planning. Cities do not feel safe because of blue LED lights, mist machines, or grand promenades; they feel safe because of active human presence.

The precinct surrounding Jalan Tun Perak operates under a rigid monoculture. Most of its banks, restaurants, and offices lock their doors by 7pm. The Masjid Jamek station functions merely as a transit hub to pass through quickly rather than a destination to inhabit. Once the peak commute closes, the street-level economy collapses into darkness.
The solution: put residents first

To fix the heart of Kuala Lumpur, we must stop treating it as a static museum or tourist backdrop and start treating it as a living neighbourhood. The most effective way to reverse this decay is to bring residents back into the historic core.

Melbourne’s revival: In the 1980s, downtown Melbourne was a desolate “donut city”. By converting underutilised commercial buildings into apartments, permitting laneway cafes and enforcing active ground-floor frontages, Melbourne transformed its centre into a vibrant downtown.

New York’s Lower Manhattan: Following economic shifts that left Wall Street deserted at night, the city introduced the 421-g tax incentive, offering exemptions to developers converting offices into apartments.

Seoul’s Cheonggyecheon strategy: the city restored the Cheonggyecheon stream and paired public space reclamation with incentives for dense residential construction, successfully reintroducing residents into its historic centre.
Local precedents and the power of housing

Kuala Lumpur has already experimented with similar concepts. Initiatives like Perumahan Bandar @ Jalan TAR show how centrally located, affordable housing can be created through adaptive reuse. Another Kuala Lumpur City Council (DBKL) project, Residensi Belia Cheras beside LRT Cheras, shows these ideas exist locally; they simply need to be scaled toward the historic grid.
We must develop affordable infill housing on surface carparks and vacant lots, while refurbishing the upper floors of historic shophouses into functional apartments.

A permanent residential population creates what urban theorist Jane Jacobs called “eyes on the street”. People sit, eat and relax at mamak shops. Children run around because it feels safe. The night becomes alive. Furthermore, residents provide the baseline demand to support an 18-hour local economy, encouraging convenience stores, laundromats and late-night eateries to keep ground-floor frontages lit and active.
Policy tools and leadership

Achieving this vision requires bold municipal leadership. Many ageing shophouses are trapped in estate disputes or held by absentee landlords content to leave properties as storage. The housing and local government ministry, alongside DBKL, must step in with clear policy tools: offering tax incentives and streamlined building codes for heritage adaptive reuse, while penalising overcrowding and land banking on derelict properties.

Infill developments on parking lots should be planned as high-density, low-car, mixed-income housing that capitalises on unmatched transit connectivity. Bringing young professionals, students, and long-time locals into the area ensures inclusivity rather than gentrification.

This vision aligns with wider policy discussions. Your colleague, Liew Chin Tong, has long advocated for Malaysians to move back into inner-city Kuala Lumpur, where living without a car is common sense. Similarly, legislative frameworks like the proposed Urban Renewal Act aim to unlock stagnant urban land and bring life back into hollowed-out districts.
The challenge is reframing these tools toward people-first outcomes rather than developer-first gains.
A call to action

Masjid Jamek does not need more beautification projects or temporary weekend events that leave the streets empty on a Tuesday night. Private initiatives like galleries and restaurants can only do so much. The area needs a living, breathing community that keeps the precinct alive after dark – an outcome only achievable at scale through dedicated public policy.

I urge you to champion a residential-first revitalisation policy for Kuala Lumpur’s central core. Until we put housing at the centre of downtown revitalisation, the historic heart of our city will remain a place of darkness the moment the sun goes down.
Boo Jia Cher is an FMT reader.
